docs.title: configure_logging()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def configure_logging(project_name="project", mode="tutorial") -> str:

Description: Configures and attaches a file-based logger instance for an individual CLI execution run. It creates a target directory specified by the LOG_DIR environment variable (defaulting to logs), sanitizes the project name and generation mode against unwanted characters, and establishes a uniquely timestamped log file named {safe_project}_{safe_mode}_{YYYYMMDD_HHmmss}.log. Any existing handlers (such as the import-time NullHandler) are cleared from logger, and a new logging.FileHandler formatted with %(asctime)s - %(levelname)s - %(message)s is registered.

Parameters: * project_name (str, optional): Identifier of the target repository or project. Defaults to "project". * mode (str, optional): Pipeline operation mode (e.g., "tutorial", "architecture"). Defaults to "tutorial".

Returns: * str: The absolute or relative filesystem path of the initialized .log file.

Raises: * OSError: If directory creation or log file access fails due to filesystem permission constraints.

Implementation: 

def configure_logging(project_name="project", mode="tutorial"):
    log_directory = os.getenv("LOG_DIR", "logs")
    os.makedirs(log_directory, exist_ok=True)

    # Sanitize project name for filesystem safety
    safe_project = "".join(c if c.isalnum() or c in "-_." else "_" for c in project_name)
    safe_mode = mode.replace("-", "_")
    timestamp = datetime.now().strftime("%Y%m%d_%H%M%S")
    log_file = os.path.join(log_directory, f"{safe_project}_{safe_mode}_{timestamp}.log")

    # Remove any existing handlers (e.g., NullHandler) and add the file handler
    logger.handlers.clear()
    file_handler = logging.FileHandler(log_file, encoding="utf-8")
    file_handler.setFormatter(logging.Formatter("%(asctime)s - %(levelname)s - %(message)s"))
    logger.addHandler(file_handler)

    # Log run metadata at the start of every log file
    logger.info(f"{'=' * 80}")
    logger.info(f"RUN STARTED | project={project_name} | mode={mode} | timestamp={timestamp}")
    logger.info(f"Log file: {log_file}")
    logger.info(f"{'=' * 80}")

    return log_file

The function performs input sanitation on project_name by replacing non-alphanumeric and non-whitelisted characters (-, _, .) with underscores. It also replaces hyphens in mode with underscores. Once the FileHandler is established, the function immediately writes execution boundary headers containing metadata to verify output capture before returning the file path to the caller (such as main).

docs.title: load_cache()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def load_cache() -> dict:

Description: Loads and deserializes the persisted JSON prompt-response cache from llm_cache.json. If the file does not exist, is corrupted, or fails to parse, it logs a warning and returns an empty dictionary.

Parameters: * None.

Returns: * dict: A dictionary mapping raw prompt strings to cached LLM response text strings, or an empty dictionary if loading fails.

Raises: * No exceptions are propagated; all file I/O and JSON decoding errors are intercepted internally.

Implementation & Usage: 

def load_cache():
    try:
        with open(cache_file) as f:
            return json.load(f)
    except Exception:
        logger.warning("Failed to load cache.")
    return {}

The function provides a fault-tolerant fallback mechanism for local development caching. Any underlying I/O errors (e.g., FileNotFoundError, PermissionError, or json.JSONDecodeError) are caught silently and flagged using logger.warning, returning a fresh dictionary to prevent crashing LLM pipeline execution.

docs.title: save_cache()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def save_cache(cache: dict) -> None:

Description: Serializes and writes the provided in-memory cache dictionary back to the llm_cache.json file on disk.

Parameters: * cache (dict): The dictionary mapping prompt strings to LLM response strings to persist.

Returns: * None

Raises: * No exceptions are propagated; file writing and serialization exceptions are handled internally.

Implementation & Usage: 

def save_cache(cache):
    try:
        with open(cache_file, "w") as f:
            json.dump(cache, f)
    except Exception:
        logger.warning("Failed to save cache")

The method opens cache_file in write mode and executes json.dump. If an exception occurs during serialization or file writing (for instance, disk full conditions or restricted write permissions), a warning is logged to llm_logger while allowing overall pipeline execution to continue uninterrupted.

docs.title: get_llm_provider()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def get_llm_provider() -> str | None:

Description: Resolves the active LLM provider strategy from environment variables. If LLM_PROVIDER is explicitly set, its value is returned. If omitted, it falls back to checking whether GEMINI_PROJECT_ID or GEMINI_API_KEY are defined, returning "GEMINI" if either is present.

Parameters: * None.

Returns: * str | None: The resolved provider string (e.g., "GEMINI", "OPENROUTER", "OLLAMA"), or None if unresolvable.

Implementation & Usage: 

def get_llm_provider():
    provider = os.getenv("LLM_PROVIDER")
    if not provider and (os.getenv("GEMINI_PROJECT_ID") or os.getenv("GEMINI_API_KEY")):
        provider = "GEMINI"
    # if necessary, add ANTHROPIC/OPENAI
    return provider

This function acts as the runtime provider selector for the application. It establishes Google Gemini as the implicit default when relevant API credentials exist in .env, while allowing overrides via explicit LLM_PROVIDER environment variable assignments (such as "OPENROUTER" or "OLLAMA").

docs.title: _get_openrouter_model_info()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _get_openrouter_model_info(model_id: str) -> dict | None:

Description: Queries OpenRouter's public /api/v1/models catalog to inspect capabilities, supported reasoning effort parameters, and metadata for a specific model ID. Caches the response payload in the module-level variable _openrouter_models_cache to eliminate redundant HTTP requests across calls.

Parameters: * model_id (str): The model identifier string (e.g., "anthropic/claude-3.7-sonnet").

Returns: * dict | None: A dictionary containing model metadata if located within the catalog; otherwise, None.

Raises: * No exceptions are raised; network and timeout errors result in populating an empty cache list and returning None.

Implementation & Usage: 

def _get_openrouter_model_info(model_id: str) -> dict:
    global _openrouter_models_cache
    if _openrouter_models_cache is None:
        try:
            resp = requests.get("https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/models", timeout=5)
            _openrouter_models_cache = resp.json().get("data", [])
        except Exception:
            _openrouter_models_cache = []

    return next((m for m in _openrouter_models_cache if m.get("id") == model_id), None)

The function optimizes network bandwidth and prevents rate limiting by fetching OpenRouter model data only on the initial call. It leverages Python's next() built-in with a generator expression to locate the model object matching model_id.

docs.title: get_model_context_length()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def get_model_context_length(endpoint_url: str, model_name: str, api_key: str = "") -> int:

Description: Determines the maximum token context window supported by a given endpoint and model name combination. Automatically allocates a 1,000,000-token limit for Gemini endpoints, dynamically extracts context limits from OpenRouter's model catalog for OpenRouter URLs, and defaults to 100,000 tokens for all other providers or when lookups fail.

Parameters: * endpoint_url (str): Base URL or endpoint of the LLM provider. * model_name (str): Name or ID of the target model. * api_key (str, optional): API key parameter (optional, defaults to "").

Returns: * int: The context length limit in tokens.

Raises: * No exceptions are propagated; errors fall back safely to 100000.

Implementation & Usage: 

def get_model_context_length(endpoint_url: str, model_name: str, api_key: str = "") -> int:
    default_limit = 100000
    try:
        if not endpoint_url:
            return default_limit

        if "generativelanguage.googleapis.com" in endpoint_url or "gemini" in model_name.lower():
            # Safely default to 1M tokens for Gemini models
            return 1000000

        if "openrouter.ai" in endpoint_url:
            resp = requests.get("https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/models", timeout=5)
            data = resp.json().get("data", [])
            for m in data:
                if m.get("id") == model_name:
                    return m.get("context_length", default_limit)
    except Exception as e:
        logger.warning(f"Failed to fetch context length for {model_name} at {endpoint_url}: {e}")

    return default_limit

This helper is primarily utilized during prompt chunking, file aggregation, and token budgeting across the indexing pipeline. When operating against Gemini endpoints or models containing "gemini" in their name, it returns a 1,000,000-token window. When hitting OpenRouter endpoints, it dynamically queries the model registry to retrieve exact token limits.

docs.title: _call_llm_provider()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _call_llm_provider(prompt: str, thinking_level: str | None = None) -> str:

Description: Dispatches chat completion requests to OpenAI-compatible provider endpoints such as OpenRouter or Ollama. Dynamically resolves environment variables based on LLM_PROVIDER (e.g., <PROVIDER>_MODEL, <PROVIDER>_BASE_URL, <PROVIDER>_API_KEY), formats messages under the /v1/chat/completions REST specification, applies reasoning/thinking effort payloads, executes HTTP requests with robust timeout limits, and validates response schemas.

Parameters: * prompt (str): The input user prompt text to send to the LLM. * thinking_level (str | None, optional): Reasoning intensity ("low", "medium", or "high"). Defaults to None.

Returns: * str: The generated text response extracted from choices[0].message.content.

Raises: * ValueError: If required environment variables (LLM_PROVIDER, <PROVIDER>_MODEL, <PROVIDER>_BASE_URL) are missing, if invalid JSON is returned, or if the choices attribute is missing from a 200 OK response. * Exception: Wrapper exception providing diagnostic context on HTTP errors, connection drops, request timeouts, or general network failures.

Implementation & Usage: 

def _call_llm_provider(prompt: str, thinking_level: str | None = None) -> str:
    # Read the provider from environment variable
    provider = os.environ.get("LLM_PROVIDER")
    if not provider:
        raise ValueError("LLM_PROVIDER environment variable is required")

    # Construct the names of the other environment variables
    model_var = f"{provider}_MODEL"
    base_url_var = f"{provider}_BASE_URL"
    api_key_var = f"{provider}_API_KEY"

    model = os.environ.get(model_var)
    base_url = os.environ.get(base_url_var)
    api_key = os.environ.get(api_key_var, "")

    if not model:
        raise ValueError(f"{model_var} environment variable is required")
    if not base_url:
        raise ValueError(f"{base_url_var} environment variable is required")

    url = f"{base_url.rstrip('/')}/v1/chat/completions"
    headers = {"Content-Type": "application/json"}
    if api_key:
        headers["Authorization"] = f"Bearer {api_key}"

    payload = {
        "model": model,
        "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": prompt}],
        "temperature": 0.7,
    }

    if provider == "OPENROUTER" and thinking_level:
        model_info = _get_openrouter_model_info(model)
        if model_info and "reasoning" in model_info:
            supported_efforts = model_info["reasoning"].get("supported_efforts", [])
            if thinking_level.lower() in supported_efforts:
                payload["reasoning"] = {"effort": thinking_level.lower()}
                payload["temperature"] = 1.0
            else:
                logger.warning(f"Invalid thinking level '{thinking_level}' for model {model}. Supported efforts: {supported_efforts}")
        else:
            logger.warning(f"Model {model} does not support reasoning via OpenRouter API.")

    elif provider == "OLLAMA" and thinking_level:
        payload["think"] = thinking_level.lower()
        payload["reasoning_effort"] = thinking_level.lower()
        payload["temperature"] = 1.0

    try:
        response = requests.post(url, headers=headers, json=payload, timeout=(10, 300))
        try:
            response_json = response.json()
        except (ValueError, requests.exceptions.JSONDecodeError):
            print(f"\033[93mWarning: Provider returned invalid JSON. Status Code: {response.status_code}, Response Text: {response.text}\033[0m")
            logger.warning(f"Provider returned invalid JSON. Status Code: {response.status_code}, Response Text: {response.text}")
            raise ValueError(f"Provider returned invalid JSON. Status Code: {response.status_code}") from None
        response.raise_for_status()

        if "choices" not in response_json or not response_json["choices"]:
            error_detail = response_json.get("error", response_json)
            logger.warning(f"API returned 200 but no 'choices' in response: {error_detail}")
            raise ValueError(f"API response missing 'choices' key. Response: {error_detail}")

        return response_json["choices"][0]["message"]["content"]
    except requests.exceptions.HTTPError as e:
        error_message = f"HTTP error occurred: {e}"
        try:
            error_details = response.json().get("error", "No additional details")
            error_message += f" (Details: {error_details})"
        except Exception:
            pass
        raise Exception(error_message) from e
    except requests.exceptions.ConnectionError as e:
        raise Exception(f"Failed to connect to {provider} API. Check your network connection.") from e
    except requests.exceptions.Timeout as e:
        raise Exception(f"Request to {provider} API timed out.") from e
    except requests.exceptions.RequestException as e:
        raise Exception(f"An error occurred while making the request to {provider}: {e}") from e
    except ValueError as e:
        raise Exception(f"Failed to parse response as JSON from {provider}. The server might have returned an invalid response.") from e

This function implements a generic REST integration for OpenAI-compatible LLM endpoints. It maps provider-specific reasoning flags (e.g., verifying supported_efforts via OpenRouter metadata or attaching think / reasoning_effort fields for Ollama) and automatically adjusts model temperature to 1.0 when reasoning effort is enabled. It configures a dual connection and read timeout (timeout=(10, 300)) to accommodate long generation runs and includes defensive JSON validation to catch upstream provider errors hidden within 200 OK responses.

docs.title: _call_llm_gemini()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _call_llm_gemini(prompt: str, thinking_level: str | None = None) -> str:

Description: Direct execution handler for the Google GenAI SDK (google.genai). Supports both Vertex AI authentication (via GEMINI_PROJECT_ID and GEMINI_LOCATION) and standalone Google Developer API keys (via GEMINI_API_KEY). Formats reasoning configurations by translating string levels into explicit token budgets (low: 1024, medium: 4096, high: 8192), filters non-text thought signatures from output candidate parts, and returns pure text output.

Parameters: * prompt (str): User prompt text to execute against Gemini. * thinking_level (str | None, optional): Reasoning budget intensity ("low", "medium", "high"). Defaults to None.

Returns: * str: The combined text generated by the model candidates, or an empty string if no content parts are returned.

Raises: * ValueError: If neither GEMINI_PROJECT_ID nor GEMINI_API_KEY are found in the environment.

Implementation & Usage: 

def _call_llm_gemini(prompt: str, thinking_level: str | None = None) -> str:
    if os.getenv("GEMINI_PROJECT_ID"):
        client = genai.Client(vertexai=True, project=os.getenv("GEMINI_PROJECT_ID"), location=os.getenv("GEMINI_LOCATION", "us-central1"))
    elif os.getenv("GEMINI_API_KEY"):
        client = genai.Client(api_key=os.getenv("GEMINI_API_KEY"))
    else:
        raise ValueError("Either GEMINI_PROJECT_ID or GEMINI_API_KEY must be set in the environment")
    model = os.getenv("GEMINI_MODEL", "gemini-3.7-flash")

    kwargs = {"model": model, "contents": [prompt]}

    if thinking_level:
        # Map string levels to budgets for the installed SDK version
        budget_map = {"low": 1024, "medium": 4096, "high": 8192}
        budget = budget_map.get(thinking_level.lower(), 4096)
        thinking_config = types.ThinkingConfig(include_thoughts=True, thinking_budget=budget)
        kwargs["config"] = types.GenerateContentConfig(thinking_config=thinking_config)

    response = client.models.generate_content(**kwargs)

    # Extract only text parts to avoid "non-text parts: ['thought_signature']" warnings
    if response.candidates and response.candidates[0].content.parts:
        text_parts = [part.text for part in response.candidates[0].content.parts if part.text is not None]
        return "".join(text_parts)
    return ""

The function instantiates the official genai.Client, choosing Vertex AI mode when GEMINI_PROJECT_ID is set and API Key mode otherwise. When thinking_level is provided, it configures types.ThinkingConfig with explicit token budgets to ensure compatibility with models such as gemini-3.7-flash. To prevent downstream logging warnings regarding non-text internal parts (such as thought_signature), it iterates over response.candidates[0].content.parts to filter and join only valid text segments.

docs.title: call_llm()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def call_llm(prompt: str, use_cache: bool = True, thinking_level: str | None = None) -> str:

Description: The primary public entry point for dispatching prompts to LLMs throughout the application. Handles token counting via count_tokens, logs prompt metadata and payload details, coordinates local disk cache hits and misses, measures round-trip inference latency, routes requests to _call_llm_gemini or _call_llm_provider, and stores newly generated responses in the cache.

Parameters: * prompt (str): The complete prompt string to submit to the model. * use_cache (bool, optional): Whether to check and update the local JSON cache. Defaults to True. * thinking_level (str | None, optional): Desired reasoning level ("low", "medium", "high"), or None for standard generation. Defaults to None.

Returns: * str: The textual response generated by the LLM (or retrieved from cache).

Raises: * ValueError: If provider resolution fails or if underlying provider calls fail. * Exception: Any network or provider-level errors encountered during an uncached invocation.

Implementation & Usage: 

def call_llm(prompt: str, use_cache: bool = True, thinking_level: str | None = None) -> str:
    import time

    from utils.token_utils import count_tokens

    provider = get_llm_provider()
    model = os.environ.get(f"{provider}_MODEL", os.environ.get("GEMINI_MODEL", "unknown"))
    prompt_tokens = count_tokens(prompt)

    logger.info(f"{'=' * 80}")
    logger.info(
        f"LLM CALL START | provider={provider} | model={model} | thinking={thinking_level} | cache={'enabled' if use_cache else 'disabled'} | prompt_tokens={prompt_tokens:,}"
    )
    logger.info(f"PROMPT:\n{prompt}")

    # Check cache if enabled
    if use_cache:
        cache = load_cache()
        if prompt in cache:
            cached_response = cache[prompt]
            logger.info(f"CACHE HIT | response_chars={len(cached_response):,}")
            logger.info(f"RESPONSE (cached):\n{cached_response}")
            logger.info("LLM CALL END | result=cache_hit")
            return cached_response

    # Make the actual LLM call
    start_time = time.time()
    logger.info(f"API CALL | sending request to {provider}...")

    if provider == "GEMINI":
        response_text = _call_llm_gemini(prompt, thinking_level=thinking_level)
    else:  # generic method using a URL that is OpenAI compatible API (Ollama, ...)
        response_text = _call_llm_provider(prompt, thinking_level=thinking_level)

    elapsed = time.time() - start_time
    logger.info(f"API CALL COMPLETE | elapsed={elapsed:.1f}s | response_chars={len(response_text):,}")
    logger.info(f"RESPONSE:\n{response_text}")

    # Update cache if enabled
    if use_cache:
        cache = load_cache()
        cache[prompt] = response_text
        save_cache(cache)
        logger.info("CACHE WRITE | saved response to cache")

    logger.info(f"LLM CALL END | result=success | elapsed={elapsed:.1f}s")
    return response_text

Example from Module Self-Test: 

if __name__ == "__main__":
    test_prompt = "Hello, how are you?"

    # First call - should hit the API
    print("Making call...")
    response1 = call_llm(test_prompt, use_cache=False)
    print(f"Response: {response1}")

call_llm serves as the single orchestrator for all generation tasks across the framework. It ensures consistent token counting via utils.token_utils, audit logging to the run log configured in configure_logging, latency metrics, and atomic cache operations.

docs.title: call_llm.py
docs.text:
Source: utils/call_llm.py

Following the structural initialization established in utils/init.py, utils/call_llm.py implements the centralized Large Language Model (LLM) execution engine for the Codebase-Knowledge-Builder system. It abstracts model interaction across distinct AI providers, unifying direct Google Gemini SDK integrations with OpenAI-compatible REST endpoints (including OpenRouter, Ollama, and local model proxies). The module encapsulates dynamic provider routing, prompt caching, reasoning/thinking budget parameterization, token counting hooks, context window resolution, and defensive error containment.

docs.title: Technical Overview
docs.text:
The module serves as the primary inference gateway for workflow nodes in nodes.py. It mediates all outbound LLM traffic, decoupling higher-level pipeline orchestration from provider-specific payload schemas, authentication protocols, and error-handling semantics. The execution architecture relies on two distinct transport layers: the official Google GenAI SDK (google.genai) for native Gemini Vertex and API services, and direct HTTP transport via requests for generic OpenAI-compatible APIs (such as OpenRouter and Ollama).

A built-in JSON file caching mechanism (llm_cache.json) intercepts duplicate inference requests. Before dispatching an expensive network operation, call_llm.py checks for identical prompt inputs, short-circuiting execution upon a cache hit. The module also manages reasoning parameters across providers, translating abstract thinking levels (low, medium, high) into concrete provider payloads—such as ThinkingConfig budgets for Gemini, reasoning effort dictionaries for OpenRouter, or think/reasoning_effort fields for Ollama.

Visibility: Public Signature: def call_llm(prompt: str, use_cache: bool = True, thinking_level: str | None = None) -> str:

Description: Orchestrates the top-level execution flow for model inference. It coordinates token estimation, cache verification, dynamic provider selection, execution timing, response extraction, and cache synchronization.

docs.title: Phase 1: Provider and Token Accounting
docs.text:

The function identifies the active LLM provider via get_llm_provider() and resolves the active model identifier using environment variables. It calls count_tokens() from token_utils.py to calculate prompt complexity for observability before emitting entry log records containing execution metadata.

docs.title: Phase 2: Cache Evaluation and Short-Circuiting
docs.text:
# Check cache if enabled
    if use_cache:

When use_cache is True, the local cache dictionary is loaded from disk via load_cache(). If an exact string match for prompt exists in the cache, the cached response is logged and returned immediately, avoiding network latency and token consumption.

docs.title: Phase 3: LLM Provider Dispatch and Execution
docs.text:

    start_time = time.time()

If the prompt is not cached, the execution timer starts and request dispatch branches based on the resolved provider string. If provider == "GEMINI", the internal helper _call_llm_gemini() handles invocation; otherwise, _call_llm_provider() is called for OpenAI-compatible REST endpoints. Upon completion, elapsed wall-clock time and response sizes are recorded.

docs.title: Phase 4: Cache Update and Finalization
docs.text:
# Update cache if enabled
    if use_cache:
        cache = load_cache()
        cache[prompt] = response_text
        save_cache(cache)

    logger.info(f"LLM CALL END | result=success | elapsed={elapsed:.1f}s")

If caching is enabled, the cache dictionary is reloaded from disk to account for concurrent writes, updated with the new prompt-response pair, and committed to disk via save_cache(). Finally, the raw text response is returned to the caller.

Parameters: * prompt (str): The complete input prompt text submitted to the language model. * use_cache (bool, optional): Flag controlling whether to read from and write to the local llm_cache.json file. Defaults to True. * thinking_level (str | None, optional): Reasoning intensity level (e.g., "low", "medium", "high"), mapped to provider-specific reasoning configurations. Defaults to None.

Returns: * str: The text response generated by the LLM.

Raises: * ValueError: If environment credentials or model configurations are invalid. * Exception: If network requests fail, connection timeouts occur, or invalid JSON is returned.

Example: 

from utils.call_llm import call_llm

response = call_llm("Explain the repository structure.", use_cache=False, thinking_level="medium")

docs.title: get_llm_provider()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def get_llm_provider() -> str | None:

Description: Determines the active LLM backend provider by inspecting system environment variables. It checks for an explicit LLM_PROVIDER declaration, falling back to "GEMINI" if Google Cloud credentials (GEMINI_PROJECT_ID or GEMINI_API_KEY) are present in the runtime environment.

def get_llm_provider():
    provider = os.getenv("LLM_PROVIDER")
    if not provider and (os.getenv("GEMINI_PROJECT_ID") or os.getenv("GEMINI_API_KEY")):
        provider = "GEMINI"
    # if necessary, add ANTHROPIC/OPENAI
    return provider

This helper centralizes provider resolution across utility and graph components. If no explicit LLM_PROVIDER variable is exported, the presence of standard Gemini environment variables automatically configures the Gemini backend. If no compatible provider environment variables are detected, None is returned.

Parameters: * None

Returns: * str | None: The resolved provider string (such as "GEMINI", "OPENROUTER", or "OLLAMA"), or None if unresolvable.

Raises: * None

Example: 

provider = get_llm_provider()
model = os.environ.get(f"{provider}_MODEL", os.environ.get("GEMINI_MODEL", "unknown"))

docs.title: get_model_context_length()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def get_model_context_length(endpoint_url: str, model_name: str, api_key: str = "") -> int:

Description: Resolves the maximum input context window size (in tokens) for a specified model and endpoint. It applies heuristic defaults for Gemini models, dynamically queries the OpenRouter /api/v1/models catalog when targeting OpenRouter infrastructure, and falls back to a safe default of 100,000 tokens for unrecognized endpoints.

docs.title: Phase 1: Endpoint Analysis and Heuristic Resolution
docs.text:
default_limit = 100000
    try:
        if not endpoint_url:
            return default_limit

        if "generativelanguage.googleapis.com" in endpoint_url or "gemini" in model_name.lower():
            # Safely default to 1M tokens for Gemini models
            return 1000000
The function establishes a standard baseline context window of 100,000 tokens. If the endpoint contains Google Generative Language URLs or if the model name indicates a Gemini model, it allocates a 1,000,000-token limit to match standard Gemini 1.5/2.0/3.7 context architectures.

docs.title: Phase 2: Remote OpenRouter Query and Exception Fallback
docs.text:
if "openrouter.ai" in endpoint_url:
            resp = requests.get("https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/models", timeout=5)
            data = resp.json().get("data", [])
            for m in data:
                if m.get("id") == model_name:
                    return m.get("context_length", default_limit)
    except Exception as e:
        logger.warning(f"Failed to fetch context length for {model_name} at {endpoint_url}: {e}")

    return default_limit
When communicating with OpenRouter (openrouter.ai), the function executes a GET request to https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/models with a 5-second timeout. It iterates over the returned model catalog, matching model_name against the model ID to extract its official context_length. If any network, JSON decoding, or key error occurs, a warning is logged and default_limit (100,000) is returned.

Parameters: * endpoint_url (str): Base URL or endpoint URI of the target model service. * model_name (str): Identifier of the target model (e.g., "anthropic/claude-3.7-sonnet", "gemini-3.7-flash"). * api_key (str, optional): Authorization key for protected endpoints. Defaults to "".

Returns: * int: Maximum context window capacity in tokens.

Raises: * None (All internal exceptions are caught, logged, and return the safe fallback limit).

Example: 

limit = get_model_context_length("https://openrouter.ai/api/v1", "anthropic/claude-3.7-sonnet")

docs.title: load_cache()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def load_cache() -> dict:

Description: Reads and deserializes the local JSON prompt cache file (llm_cache.json) into an in-memory dictionary.

def load_cache():
    try:
        with open(cache_file) as f:
            return json.load(f)
    except Exception:
        logger.warning("Failed to load cache.")
    return {}

The function attempts to open the file defined by module-level cache_file ("llm_cache.json"). If the file is missing, inaccessible, or corrupted, the failure is recorded to logger.warning and an empty dictionary {} is returned.

Parameters: * None

Returns: * dict: Dictionary mapping prompt strings to previously cached text responses.

Raises: * None

Example: 

cache = load_cache()
if prompt in cache:
    cached_response = cache[prompt]

docs.title: save_cache()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def save_cache(cache: dict) -> None:

Description: Serializes and writes an in-memory prompt-response dictionary to llm_cache.json.

def save_cache(cache):
    try:
        with open(cache_file, "w") as f:
            json.dump(cache, f)
    except Exception:
        logger.warning("Failed to save cache")

The function opens the file target in write mode and executes json.dump(). Any I/O errors or serialization exceptions are caught and logged as warnings, preventing transient disk failures from terminating the workflow.

Parameters: * cache (dict): The prompt-response mapping to persist to disk.

Returns: * None

Raises: * None

Example: 

cache = load_cache()
cache[prompt] = response_text
save_cache(cache)

docs.title: _call_llm_gemini()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _call_llm_gemini(prompt: str, thinking_level: str | None = None) -> str:

Description: Handles model invocation via the official Google GenAI SDK (google.genai). It configures client authentication via Vertex AI or API key credentials, maps string thinking levels to token budgets, executes generation, and extracts text segments while discarding non-text response parts.

docs.title: Phase 1: Client Initialization and Authentication Routing
docs.text:
def _call_llm_gemini(prompt: str, thinking_level: str | None = None) -> str:
    if os.getenv("GEMINI_PROJECT_ID"):
        client = genai.Client(vertexai=True, project=os.getenv("GEMINI_PROJECT_ID"), location=os.getenv("GEMINI_LOCATION", "us-central1"))
    elif os.getenv("GEMINI_API_KEY"):
        client = genai.Client(api_key=os.getenv("GEMINI_API_KEY"))
    else:
        raise ValueError("Either GEMINI_PROJECT_ID or GEMINI_API_KEY must be set in the environment")
    model = os.getenv("GEMINI_MODEL", "gemini-3.7-flash")

    kwargs = {"model": model, "contents": [prompt]}
The helper checks for GEMINI_PROJECT_ID to initialize a Vertex AI client instance configured with GEMINI_LOCATION (defaulting to "us-central1"). If absent, it checks for GEMINI_API_KEY to initialize a standard API key client. If neither is present, it raises a ValueError. The target model defaults to "gemini-3.7-flash".

docs.title: Phase 2: Thinking Budget Configuration
docs.text:
if thinking_level:
        # Map string levels to budgets for the installed SDK version
        budget_map = {"low": 1024, "medium": 4096, "high": 8192}
        budget = budget_map.get(thinking_level.lower(), 4096)
        thinking_config = types.ThinkingConfig(include_thoughts=True, thinking_budget=budget)
        kwargs["config"] = types.GenerateContentConfig(thinking_config=thinking_config)
When thinking_level is supplied, it maps the level string ("low", "medium", "high") to token limits (1024, 4096, 8192, defaulting to 4096). It creates a types.ThinkingConfig with include_thoughts=True and wraps it in a types.GenerateContentConfig, passing it to the request keyword arguments.

docs.title: Phase 3: Model Execution and Clean Text Extraction
docs.text:
response = client.models.generate_content(**kwargs)

    # Extract only text parts to avoid "non-text parts: ['thought_signature']" warnings
    if response.candidates and response.candidates[0].content.parts:
        text_parts = [part.text for part in response.candidates[0].content.parts if part.text is not None]
        return "".join(text_parts)
    return ""
The client executes generate_content(**kwargs). To handle Gemini 2.0/3.7 responses that return multiple content parts containing reasoning blocks (thought_signature), it filters the candidates' parts, concatenating only entries where part.text is not None. If no valid candidates or parts are returned, an empty string is returned.

Parameters: * prompt (str): The prompt payload to process. * thinking_level (str | None, optional): Reasoning configuration identifier ("low", "medium", "high"). Defaults to None.

Returns: * str: The combined text response generated by the Gemini model.

Raises: * ValueError: If neither GEMINI_PROJECT_ID nor GEMINI_API_KEY is configured in the environment.

Example: 

if provider == "GEMINI":
    response_text = _call_llm_gemini(prompt, thinking_level=thinking_level)

docs.title: _call_llm_provider()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _call_llm_provider(prompt: str, thinking_level: str | None = None) -> str:

Description: Dispatches chat completion requests to OpenAI-compatible HTTP REST APIs (such as OpenRouter or Ollama). It validates environment configurations, formats request headers, constructs payloads with provider-specific reasoning flags, executes the HTTP POST request with dual connect/read timeouts, and validates the response JSON structure.

docs.title: Phase 1: Environment Variable Resolution and Validation
docs.text:
def _call_llm_provider(prompt: str, thinking_level: str | None = None) -> str:
    # Read the provider from environment variable
    provider = os.environ.get("LLM_PROVIDER")
    if not provider:
        raise ValueError("LLM_PROVIDER environment variable is required")

    # Construct the names of the other environment variables
    model_var = f"{provider}_MODEL"
    base_url_var = f"{provider}_BASE_URL"
    api_key_var = f"{provider}_API_KEY"

    # Read the provider-specific variables
    model = os.environ.get(model_var)
    base_url = os.environ.get(base_url_var)
    api_key = os.environ.get(api_key_var, "")  # API key is optional, default to empty string

    # Validate required variables
    if not model:
        raise ValueError(f"{model_var} environment variable is required")
    if not base_url:
        raise ValueError(f"{base_url_var} environment variable is required")
The helper reads LLM_PROVIDER and constructs dynamic environment variable keys (<PROVIDER>_MODEL, <PROVIDER>_BASE_URL, <PROVIDER>_API_KEY). It verifies that both the model and base URL are set, raising a ValueError if either variable is missing.

docs.title: Phase 2: Payload Construction and Reasoning Configuration
docs.text:
# Append the endpoint to the base URL
    url = f"{base_url.rstrip('/')}/v1/chat/completions"

    # Configure headers and payload based on provider
    headers = {
        "Content-Type": "application/json",
    }
    if api_key:  # Only add Authorization header if API key is provided
        headers["Authorization"] = f"Bearer {api_key}"

    payload = {
        "model": model,
        "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": prompt}],
        "temperature": 0.7,
    }

    if provider == "OPENROUTER" and thinking_level:
        model_info = _get_openrouter_model_info(model)
        if model_info and "reasoning" in model_info:
            supported_efforts = model_info["reasoning"].get("supported_efforts", [])
            if thinking_level.lower() in supported_efforts:
                payload["reasoning"] = {"effort": thinking_level.lower()}
                payload["temperature"] = 1.0  # Required for many reasoning models
            else:
                logger.warning(f"Invalid thinking level '{thinking_level}' for model {model}. Supported efforts: {supported_efforts}")
        else:
            logger.warning(f"Model {model} does not support reasoning via OpenRouter API.")

    elif provider == "OLLAMA" and thinking_level:
        # Some Ollama SDKs / API versions look for `think`, others look for standard `reasoning_effort`
        payload["think"] = thinking_level.lower()
        payload["reasoning_effort"] = thinking_level.lower()
        payload["temperature"] = 1.0
The endpoint URL is constructed by appending /v1/chat/completions to the base URL. If thinking_level is requested for OpenRouter, the helper checks cached model metadata via _get_openrouter_model_info(). If reasoning is supported, it injects payload["reasoning"] = {"effort": thinking_level.lower()} and adjusts the temperature to 1.0. For Ollama, it sets both payload["think"] and payload["reasoning_effort"] alongside temperature = 1.0.

docs.title: Phase 3: Network Execution, Error Interception, and Response Parsing
docs.text:
try:
        response = requests.post(url, headers=headers, json=payload, timeout=(10, 300))
        try:
            response_json = response.json()  # Log the response
        except (ValueError, requests.exceptions.JSONDecodeError):
            from utils.output import emit_raw

            emit_raw(
                "WARNING",
                f"Warning: Provider returned invalid JSON. Status Code: {response.status_code}, Response Text: {response.text}",
                dest="STDOUT",
            )
            logger.warning(f"Provider returned invalid JSON. Status Code: {response.status_code}, Response Text: {response.text}")
            raise ValueError(f"Provider returned invalid JSON. Status Code: {response.status_code}") from None
        response.raise_for_status()

        # Defensive check: API may return 200 with error/rate-limit payload missing 'choices'
        if "choices" not in response_json or not response_json["choices"]:
            error_detail = response_json.get("error", response_json)
            logger.warning(f"API returned 200 but no 'choices' in response: {error_detail}")
            raise ValueError(f"API response missing 'choices' key. Response: {error_detail}")

        return response_json["choices"][0]["message"]["content"]
    except requests.exceptions.HTTPError as e:
        error_message = f"HTTP error occurred: {e}"
        try:
            error_details = response.json().get("error", "No additional details")
            error_message += f" (Details: {error_details})"
        except Exception:
            pass
        raise Exception(error_message) from e
    except requests.exceptions.ConnectionError as e:
        raise Exception(f"Failed to connect to {provider} API. Check your network connection.") from e
    except requests.exceptions.Timeout as e:
        raise Exception(f"Request to {provider} API timed out.") from e
    except requests.exceptions.RequestException as e:
        raise Exception(f"An error occurred while making the request to {provider}: {e}") from e
    except ValueError as e:
        raise Exception(f"Failed to parse response as JSON from {provider}. The server might have returned an invalid response.") from e
The request is dispatched with a connection timeout of 10 seconds and a read timeout of 300 seconds. If parsing fails, an alert is dispatched through emit_raw() from output.py. The helper also handles edge cases where providers return an HTTP 200 status code containing rate-limit or error messages without a choices array.

Parameters: * prompt (str): Prompt text submitted to the provider. * thinking_level (str | None, optional): Reasoning intensity string. Defaults to None.

Returns: * str: Extracted response content from choices[0].message.content.

Raises: * ValueError: If required environment variables are unset or the response payload is malformed. * Exception: On network connection failures, request timeouts, or HTTP status errors.

Example: 

else:  # generic method using a URL that is OpenAI compatible API (Ollama, ...)
    response_text = _call_llm_provider(prompt, thinking_level=thinking_level)

docs.title: _get_openrouter_model_info()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _get_openrouter_model_info(model_id: str) -> dict | None:

Description: Retrieves model metadata from the OpenRouter catalog (https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/models). It uses a module-level cache variable _openrouter_models_cache to avoid repeated remote network lookups during a workflow run.

def _get_openrouter_model_info(model_id: str) -> dict:
    global _openrouter_models_cache
    if _openrouter_models_cache is None:
        try:
            resp = requests.get("https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/models", timeout=5)
            _openrouter_models_cache = resp.json().get("data", [])
        except Exception:
            _openrouter_models_cache = []

    return next((m for m in _openrouter_models_cache if m.get("id") == model_id), None)

When first invoked, the helper fetches the active models catalog from OpenRouter with a 5-second timeout. If the request fails, _openrouter_models_cache is set to an empty list []. Subsequent queries filter this in-memory list by model ID.

Parameters: * model_id (str): OpenRouter model identifier (e.g., "deepseek/deepseek-r1").

Returns: * dict | None: The model metadata dictionary if found, or None.

Raises: * None

Example: 

model_info = _get_openrouter_model_info(model)
if model_info and "reasoning" in model_info:
    supported_efforts = model_info["reasoning"].get("supported_efforts", [])

docs.title: Error Handling
docs.text:
utils/call_llm.py implements defensive error-handling patterns across both transport layers:

  1. Missing Configuration Verification: Before initiating network calls, the module validates that required provider variables (LLM_PROVIDER, <PROVIDER>_MODEL, <PROVIDER>_BASE_URL, or GEMINI_PROJECT_ID/GEMINI_API_KEY) are present. Missing parameters immediately raise a descriptive ValueError.

  2. Defensive Response and Content Parsing: When communicating with generic HTTP endpoints, the module checks for non-standard failure modes:

  3. Invalid JSON Payloads: If a proxy or endpoint returns non-JSON data (e.g., HTML 502 Bad Gateway responses), the error is caught, surfaced to standard output using emit_raw() from output.py, logged to llm_logger, and re-raised as a ValueError.

  4. Missing choices Array: Some APIs return HTTP 200 OK statuses containing error or rate-limiting details in the root JSON object instead of a valid choices array. The module verifies that "choices" exists and is non-empty before indexing into choices[0].

  5. HTTP Transport Exception Wrapping: All requests.exceptions subclasses are caught and wrapped in standard Python Exception types with context-specific messages:

  6. requests.exceptions.HTTPError: Extracts nested error details from response JSON when available.
  7. requests.exceptions.ConnectionError: Returns a clear message prompting the user to check network configurations.

  8. requests.exceptions.Timeout: Flags requests exceeding the 10-second connect or 300-second read timeouts.

  9. Multi-Part Gemini Thought Segment Filtering: The Gemini SDK may return thought segments alongside generation text. In _call_llm_gemini(), the response candidate parts are filtered using [part.text for part in parts if part.text is not None] to prevent thought_signature warnings.

  10. Fault-Tolerant Cache Operations: Both load_cache() and save_cache() wrap disk I/O operations in general try...except blocks. If disk permissions or serialization fail, operations log a warning and return empty state rather than terminating the workflow.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The utils.crawl_github_files module provides repository ingestion capabilities for GitHub repositories within the Codebase-Knowledge-Builder architecture. It is designed to extract codebase contents across public and private repositories, handling two distinct ingestion paths based on the input URL format:

  1. SSH Git Cloning Mode: Activated when the target URL starts with git@ or ends with .git. It clones the repository into an isolated temporary directory via GitPython (git.Repo.clone_from), walks the local directory structure, enforces file inclusion/exclusion and .gitignore rules using pathspec, and reads text content directly from disk.
  2. GitHub REST API Mode: Activated for standard HTTP/HTTPS URLs (e.g., https://github.com/owner/repo/tree/ref/path). It parses the URL into structural components (owner, repository name, branch or tree SHA, and targeted subdirectory path). It queries the GitHub REST API (/repos/{owner}/{repo}/contents/{path}), handles dynamic branch and commit tree resolution, fetches repository-level .gitignore rules, performs automatic rate-limit backoff using HTTP headers (X-RateLimit-Reset), and downloads raw or base64-encoded file payloads.

Both paths enforce strict file size filtering (max_file_size), text-encoding checks (handling UTF-8 with BOM and binary file detection), glob pattern matching via fnmatch, path rebasing (use_relative_paths), and return a normalized dictionary mapping file paths to their string contents alongside crawl statistics.

docs.title: crawl_github_files()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def crawl_github_files(repo_url, token=None, max_file_size: int = 1 * 1024 * 1024, use_relative_paths: bool = False, include_patterns: str | set[str] | None = None, exclude_patterns: str | set[str] | None = None) -> dict:

Description: Serves as the primary public entry point for extracting text files from a remote GitHub repository. The function standardizes pattern collections, detects whether to utilize SSH cloning or the GitHub REST API, evaluates inclusion/exclusion patterns alongside .gitignore path specifications, downloads or reads files under the size threshold, and compiles a comprehensive execution summary.

Parameters: * repo_url (str): The remote URL of the GitHub repository. Supports full HTTPS tree paths (e.g., https://github.com/microsoft/autogen/tree/commit_hash/sub/path) or SSH URLs (e.g., git@github.com:owner/repo.git). * token (str, optional): GitHub personal access token used to authorize private repository access and lift public REST API rate limits. Defaults to None. * max_file_size (int, optional): Maximum allowed size in bytes per file (default is 1 MB: 1048576 bytes). Files exceeding this limit are skipped. * use_relative_paths (bool, optional): When True, returns dictionary keys stripped of the leading subdirectory path specified in the URL. Defaults to False. * include_patterns (str | set[str] | None, optional): Glob pattern or set of glob patterns (e.g., "*.py", {"*.md", "*.txt"}) indicating which file names should be retained. If None, all files are candidates. * exclude_patterns (str | set[str] | None, optional): Glob pattern or set of glob patterns indicating which file or directory paths should be skipped.

Returns: * dict: A dictionary containing two keys: * "files" (dict[str, str]): Mapping of resolved file paths to their decoded string file content. * "stats" (dict): Execution metadata containing counts of downloaded files, skipped files, active filter patterns, and base path configurations.

Raises: * ValueError: Raised if the provided HTTP URL cannot be split into at least owner and repo components. * Exception: Raised when GitHub API rate limits are hit without an authorization token provided.

Example: 

# Extract from example usage in utils/crawl_github_files.py
repo_url = "https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/tree/6c38dc93f40a47f4d1350adca9ec0d72502e223f/pydantic"

result = crawl_github_files(
    repo_url,
    token=github_token,
    max_file_size=1 * 1024 * 1024,  # 1 MB in bytes
    use_relative_paths=True,  # Enable relative paths
    include_patterns={"*.py", "*.md"},  # Include Python and Markdown files
)

files = result["files"]
stats = result["stats"]

The function normalizes inputs into sets, sets up pattern matching closures, and dynamically routes between temporary disk cloning via Git and in-memory REST API tree traversal. When operating in REST API mode, it resolves branch names and commit SHAs dynamically, falling back to repository defaults when no tree parameters are supplied in the URL.

docs.title: should_include_file()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private / Internal Helper (nested within crawl_github_files) Signature: def should_include_file(file_path: str, file_name: str, gitignore_spec=None) -> bool:

Description: Evaluates whether a candidate file matches the current execution criteria based on file name glob inclusions, repository .gitignore specifications, and explicit path exclusions.

Parameters: * file_path (str): The relative path of the file within the repository or cloned working tree. * file_name (str): The base name of the file (e.g., main.py). * gitignore_spec (pathspec.PathSpec, optional): Compiled gitignore rules specifier instantiated using pathspec.PathSpec.from_lines('gitwildmatch', ...). Defaults to None.

Returns: * bool: True if the file satisfies include filters, does not match .gitignore, and is not excluded by exclude_patterns; otherwise False.

Example: 

    def should_include_file(file_path: str, file_name: str, gitignore_spec=None) -> bool:
        """Determine if a file should be included based on patterns"""
        # If no include patterns are specified, include all files
        if not include_patterns:
            include_file = True
        else:
            # Check if file matches any include pattern
            include_file = any(fnmatch.fnmatch(file_name, pattern) for pattern in include_patterns)

        # Check gitignore if provided
        if include_file and gitignore_spec and gitignore_spec.match_file(file_path):
            return False

        # If exclude patterns are specified, check if file should be excluded
        if exclude_patterns and include_file:
            # Exclude if file matches any exclude pattern
            exclude_file = any(fnmatch.fnmatch(file_path, pattern) for pattern in exclude_patterns)
            return not exclude_file

        return include_file

The inclusion evaluation follows a three-stage gating sequence. First, if include_patterns is populated, the file's basename must match at least one pattern via fnmatch.fnmatch. Second, if a compiled gitignore_spec is provided, gitignore_spec.match_file(file_path) checks the full relative path; any match immediately disqualifies the file. Finally, if exclude_patterns is defined, the full relative path is matched against all exclusion globs.

docs.title: fetch_branches()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private / Internal Helper (nested within crawl_github_files) Signature: def fetch_branches(owner: str, repo: str) -> list[dict]:

Description: Queries the GitHub REST API endpoint /repos/{owner}/{repo}/branches to obtain a list of all remote branches available on the target repository. This information is used to match multi-part branch names (e.g., feature/branch-name) present within complex repository URLs.

Parameters: * owner (str): The GitHub account or organization name hosting the repository. * repo (str): The repository name.

Returns: * list[dict]: A list of branch descriptor dictionaries returned by GitHub's API, or an empty list [] if the repository was not found or an HTTP error occurred.

Raises: * Exception: Raised if HTTP status code 403 or 429 is received and no GitHub token was configured.

Example: 

    def fetch_branches(owner: str, repo: str):
        """Get brancshes of the repository"""

        url = f"https://api.github.com/repos/{owner}/{repo}/branches"
        response = requests.get(url, headers=headers, timeout=(30, 30))

        if response.status_code in (403, 429) and not token:
            raise Exception("GitHub API rate limit exceeded. Please provide a GitHub token using --token or GITHUB_TOKEN env var.")

        if response.status_code == 404:
            if not token:
                print(
                    "Error 404: Repository not found or is private.\n"
                    "If this is a private repository, please provide a valid GitHub token via the 'token' argument or set the GITHUB_TOKEN environment variable."
                )
            else:
                print(
                    "Error 404: Repository not found or insufficient permissions with the provided token.\n"
                    "Please verify the repository exists and the token has access to this repository."
                )
            return []

        if response.status_code != 200:
            print(f"Error fetching the branches of {owner}/{repo}: {response.status_code} - {response.text}")
            return []

        return response.json()

The function transmits an authorized GET request with a strict 30-second connection and read timeout. It verifies status codes, explicitly separating rate-limit exhaustion (403/429), missing or unauthorized repositories (404), and general server or network errors before parsing JSON results.

docs.title: check_tree()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private / Internal Helper (nested within crawl_github_files) Signature: def check_tree(owner: str, repo: str, tree: str) -> bool:

Description: Verifies whether a given commit SHA or Git tree identifier exists on the remote repository by querying /repos/{owner}/{repo}/git/trees/{tree}.

Parameters: * owner (str): The GitHub account or organization name. * repo (str): The repository name. * tree (str): The tree SHA, commit hash, or tag to validate.

Returns: * bool: True if the tree object exists (HTTP status 200); False otherwise.

Raises: * Exception: Raised when GitHub API rate limits are exceeded in unauthenticated mode.

Example: 

    def check_tree(owner: str, repo: str, tree: str):
        """Check the repository has the given tree"""

        url = f"https://api.github.com/repos/{owner}/{repo}/git/trees/{tree}"
        response = requests.get(url, headers=headers, timeout=(30, 30))

        if response.status_code in (403, 429) and not token:
            raise Exception("GitHub API rate limit exceeded. Please provide a GitHub token using --token or GITHUB_TOKEN env var.")

        return response.status_code == 200

This helper handles scenarios where a URL points directly to an immutable Git tree or commit SHA rather than a named branch (e.g., /tree/e45a15766746...). By checking the Git Trees API directly, it validates commit-specific checkouts without having to iterate through all repository branches.

Description: Reconstructs a subpath string by joining URL path segments starting from an integer index i through the end of the path_parts list.

Parameters: * i (int): Starting index within the parsed URL path segment list path_parts.

Returns: * str: Slash-delimited path segment.

Example:

The function serves as a utility during URL segment resolution. docs.title: fetch_contents()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private / Internal Helper (nested within crawl_github_files) Signature: def fetch_contents(path: str) -> None:

Description: Recursively fetches and processes directory contents and files from the GitHub REST API (/repos/{owner}/{repo}/contents/{path}). It handles rate-limit backoff, skips excluded directories and oversized files, downloads raw file contents via download_url or decodes base64 content blocks, and populates the outer files dictionary.

Parameters: * path (str): Repository-relative subdirectory or file path to query against the GitHub Contents API.

Returns: * None: Mutates the enclosing scope's files dictionary and api_counters state in-place.

Raises: * Exception: Raised if unauthenticated rate limits are encountered during directory retrieval.

Example: 

    def fetch_contents(path):
        """Fetch contents of the repository at a specific path and commit"""
        url = f"https://api.github.com/repos/{owner}/{repo}/contents/{path}"
        params = {"ref": ref} if ref is not None else {}

        response = requests.get(url, headers=headers, params=params, timeout=(30, 30))

        if response.status_code in (403, 429) and "rate limit exceeded" in response.text.lower():
            if not token:
                raise Exception("GitHub API rate limit exceeded. Please provide a GitHub token using --token or GITHUB_TOKEN env var.")
            reset_time = int(response.headers.get("X-RateLimit-Reset", 0))
            wait_time = max(reset_time - time.time(), 0) + 1
            print(f"Rate limit exceeded. Waiting for {wait_time:.0f} seconds...")
            time.sleep(wait_time)
            return fetch_contents(path)

        if response.status_code == 404:
            // ... [Handle 404 and branch warning messages]
            return None

        if response.status_code != 200:
            print(f"Error fetching {path}: {response.status_code} - {response.text}")
            return None

        contents = response.json()
        if not isinstance(contents, list):
            contents = [contents]

        for item in contents:
            item_path = item["path"]
            // ... [Calculate rel_path, check filters, download raw/base64 content, recurse dirs]

fetch_contents performs recursive crawling over the GitHub API tree. If a rate limit is reached for an authenticated user, it inspects the X-RateLimit-Reset Unix timestamp from GitHub's response headers, suspends execution via time.sleep, and retries the request automatically upon expiration. For each item returned, if the entry is a directory, it checks inclusion/exclusion patterns before executing a recursive call. If it is a file, it checks file size constraints, issues a download request via download_url (or falls back to decoding base64-encoded strings directly from the JSON metadata), and writes decoded text directly into the outer files dictionary.

docs.title: crawl_github_files.py
docs.text:
Source: utils/crawl_github_files.py

Following the inference abstraction layer documented in call_llm.py, utils/crawl_github_files.py implements the remote repository ingestion engine for the Codebase-Knowledge-Builder system. While model inference consumes standardized text representations of source code, this module is responsible for extracting, filtering, and normalizing those source files directly from remote GitHub repositories.

docs.title: Technical Overview
docs.text:
utils/crawl_github_files.py provides a dual-engine architecture for ingesting source code from GitHub repositories without requiring manual local repository configuration. It supports both public and private repositories, handling deep URL subpath specifications, specific Git commits, tree references, and branch names. The module evaluates remote repository content against inclusion patterns, exclusion lists, file size limits, and .gitignore specifications, returning a standardized in-memory dictionary mapping file paths to their UTF-8 string contents.

The module operates across two distinct execution strategies: 1. Git over SSH Clone Engine: Triggered when a URL starts with git@ or ends with .git. The module provisions an ephemeral directory via Python's tempfile.TemporaryDirectory, performs a shallow clone using GitPython (git.Repo.clone_from), parses any top-level .gitignore via pathspec, and performs a filtered filesystem walk before releasing all disk resources. 2. GitHub REST API Engine: Utilized for standard HTTPS GitHub URLs (e.g., https://github.com/owner/repo/tree/commit/subpath). The engine parses the URL into its constituent components (owner, repository name, branch/commit ref, and subdirectory path), validates refs against the /branches and /git/trees endpoints, loads remote .gitignore definitions via Base64 decoding, and recursively traverses the directory tree using the /contents API.

To protect the execution environment against resource exhaustion and rate degradation, the module incorporates automatic HTTP 403/429 rate-limit backoff using GitHub's X-RateLimit-Reset headers, enforces binary/non-text file detection, applies a default 1 MB per-file size ceiling, and streams execution progress events to the console via output.py.
