docs.title: crawl_github_files()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def crawl_github_files(repo_url: str, token: str | None = None, max_file_size: int = 1 * 1024 * 1024, use_relative_paths: bool = False, include_patterns: str | set[str] | None = None, exclude_patterns: str | set[str] | None = None) -> dict:

Description: Main entry point for crawling a remote GitHub repository. Evaluates the URL scheme to dispatch execution between the Git SSH clone strategy and the GitHub REST API v3 recursive traversal strategy. Both strategies apply path matching, gitignore filtering, file size validation, text decoding, and progress telemetry before returning a unified dictionary mapping file paths to their string contents.

Parameters: * repo_url (str): URL of the GitHub repository. Supports standard HTTPS URLs with commit/branch and subpath components (e.g., https://github.com/owner/repo/tree/main/sub/dir) or SSH clone URLs (e.g., git@github.com:owner/repo.git). * token (str | None, optional): GitHub Personal Access Token (PAT). Required for private repositories and recommended for public repositories to avoid rate-limiting ceilings (60 requests/hr unauthenticated vs. 5,000 requests/hr authenticated). Defaults to None. * max_file_size (int, optional): Maximum individual file size in bytes to download and ingest into memory. Defaults to 1048576 (1 MB). * use_relative_paths (bool, optional): If True, file paths in the returned dictionary are calculated relative to the specified subpath rather than the root of the repository. Defaults to False. * include_patterns (str | set[str] | None, optional): Glob pattern or set of glob patterns specifying which file names to include (e.g., *.py or {"*.py", "*.md"}). If None, all files are eligible. Defaults to None. * exclude_patterns (str | set[str] | None, optional): Glob pattern or set of glob patterns specifying directory names or file paths to exclude. If None, no explicit exclude rules are applied. Defaults to None.

Returns: * dict: A dictionary containing the populated files mapping and associated crawling stats metadata. See Data Structures for structural specifications.

Raises: * ValueError: If the provided HTTPS GitHub URL contains fewer than two path components (owner/repo). * Exception: If the unauthenticated rate limit is exhausted during API queries or Git clone operations encounter fatal transport errors.

docs.title: Phase 1: Parameter Normalization and Pattern Setup
docs.text:
Normalizes string-based include and exclude patterns into uniform Python set collections to ensure consistent iteration and lookup semantics throughout the crawling lifecycle.

    # Convert single pattern to set
    if include_patterns and isinstance(include_patterns, str):
        include_patterns = {include_patterns}
    if exclude_patterns and isinstance(exclude_patterns, str):
        exclude_patterns = {exclude_patterns}

    def should_include_file(file_path: str, file_name: str, gitignore_spec=None) -> bool:
        """Determine if a file should be included based on patterns"""
        # If no include patterns are specified, include all files
        if not include_patterns:
            include_file = True
        else:
            # Check if file matches any include pattern
            include_file = any(fnmatch.fnmatch(file_name, pattern) for pattern in include_patterns)

        # Check gitignore if provided
        if include_file and gitignore_spec and gitignore_spec.match_file(file_path):
            return False

        # If exclude patterns are specified, check if file should be excluded
        if exclude_patterns and include_file:
            # Exclude if file matches any exclude pattern
            exclude_file = any(fnmatch.fnmatch(file_path, pattern) for pattern in exclude_patterns)
            return not exclude_file

        return include_file

The function standardizes include_patterns and exclude_patterns into Python set structures if passed as scalar strings. It defines a nested helper closure should_include_file that encapsulates the evaluation chain: positive match against include patterns (or pass-through if unconfigured), negative check against compiled .gitignore path specifications (pathspec), and negative match against user-provided exclusion patterns.

docs.title: Phase 2: Protocol Detection and Git SSH Clone Pipeline
docs.text:
Executes when the URL string satisfies SSH format heuristics (git@ prefix or .git suffix). Clones the repository into a context-managed temporary directory and walks the filesystem on disk.

    # Detect SSH URL (git@ or .git suffix)
    is_ssh_url = repo_url.startswith("git@") or repo_url.endswith(".git")

    if is_ssh_url:
        # Clone repo via SSH to temp dir
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmpdirname:
            emit_raw("PROGRESS", f"Cloning SSH repo {repo_url} to temp dir {tmpdirname} ...")
            try:
                repo = git.Repo.clone_from(repo_url, tmpdirname)
            except Exception as e:
                emit_raw("ERROR", f"Error cloning repo: {e}")
                return {"files": {}, "stats": {"error": str(e)}}

            # Attempt to checkout specific commit/branch if in URL
            # Parse ref and subdir from SSH URL? SSH URLs don't have branch info embedded
            # So rely on default branch, or user can checkout manually later
            # Optionally, user can pass ref explicitly in future API

            # Walk directory
            files = {}

            # --- Counters ---
            count_processed = 0
            count_excluded = 0
            count_size_limit = 0
            count_non_text = 0
            skipped_size_list = []
            skipped_non_text_list = []
            entry_num = 0

            # --- Load .gitignore ---
            gitignore_path = os.path.join(tmpdirname, ".gitignore")
            gitignore_spec = None
            if os.path.exists(gitignore_path):
                try:
                    with open(gitignore_path, encoding="utf-8-sig") as f:
                        gitignore_spec = pathspec.PathSpec.from_lines("gitwildmatch", f.readlines())
                    emit("CRAWL_GITIGNORE_LOADED", path="repository")
                except Exception:
                    pass

            for root, dirs, filenames in os.walk(tmpdirname):
                # Filter directories
                excluded_dirs = set()
                for d in sorted(dirs):
                    dirpath_rel = os.path.relpath(os.path.join(root, d), tmpdirname)
                    reason = None
                    if gitignore_spec and gitignore_spec.match_file(dirpath_rel):
                        reason = get("CRAWL_REASON_GITIGNORE")
                    elif exclude_patterns:
                        for pattern in exclude_patterns:
                            dir_pattern = pattern.removesuffix("/*")
                            if fnmatch.fnmatch(dirpath_rel, dir_pattern) or fnmatch.fnmatch(d, dir_pattern):
                                reason = get("CRAWL_REASON_EXCLUDED")
                                break

                    if reason:
                        excluded_dirs.add(d)
                        entry_num += 1
                        count_excluded += 1
                        emit("CRAWL_DIR_EXCLUDED", num=entry_num, path=dirpath_rel, reason=reason)

                for d in dirs.copy():
                    if d in excluded_dirs:
                        dirs.remove(d)

                # Sort remaining dirs for consistent traversal order
                dirs.sort()

                for filename in sorted(filenames):
                    abs_path = os.path.join(root, filename)
                    rel_path = os.path.relpath(abs_path, tmpdirname)
                    entry_num += 1

                    # Check include/exclude patterns
                    if not should_include_file(rel_path, filename, gitignore_spec=gitignore_spec):
                        count_excluded += 1
                        emit("CRAWL_FILE_EXCLUDED", num=entry_num, path=rel_path)
                        continue

                    # Check file size
                    try:
                        file_size = os.path.getsize(abs_path)
                    except OSError:
                        continue

                    if file_size > max_file_size:
                        count_size_limit += 1
                        skipped_size_list.append(rel_path)
                        size_kb = file_size / 1024
                        emit("CRAWL_FILE_SIZE_LIMIT", num=entry_num, path=rel_path, size=f"{size_kb:.0f}")
                        continue

                    # Read content
                    try:
                        with open(abs_path, encoding="utf-8-sig") as f:
                            content = f.read()
                        files[rel_path] = content
                        count_processed += 1
                        emit("CRAWL_FILE_PROCESSED", num=entry_num, path=rel_path)
                    except (UnicodeDecodeError, ValueError):
                        count_non_text += 1
                        skipped_non_text_list.append(rel_path)
                        emit("CRAWL_FILE_NOT_TEXT", num=entry_num, path=rel_path)
                    except Exception as e:
                        count_non_text += 1
                        skipped_non_text_list.append(rel_path)
                        emit("CRAWL_FILE_ERROR", num=entry_num, path=rel_path, error=e)

The SSH pipeline provisions a temporary folder and invokes git.Repo.clone_from. If cloning fails, it emits an error event and returns an error payload immediately. When successful, it inspects the cloned root for a .gitignore file and compiles its lines into a pathspec.PathSpec matcher using the gitwildmatch dialect. It then invokes os.walk, pruning matched directories dynamically from dirs in-place to avoid descending into excluded branches (such as .git or build outputs). Individual files are validated against the pattern matcher and checked for size via os.path.getsize. Text files are ingested with utf-8-sig encoding handling, catching UnicodeDecodeError to skip binary assets cleanly.

docs.title: Phase 3: GitHub REST API URL Parsing and Ref Resolution
docs.text:
Handles standard HTTPS URLs by parsing path components into repository metadata, identifying commit hashes, branch names, and requested subdirectories.

    # Parse GitHub URL to extract owner, repo, commit/branch, and path
    parsed_url = urlparse(repo_url)
    path_parts = parsed_url.path.strip("/").split("/")

    if len(path_parts) < 2:
        raise ValueError(f"Invalid GitHub URL: {repo_url}")

    # Extract the basic components
    owner = path_parts[0]
    repo = path_parts[1]

    # Setup for GitHub API
    headers = {"Accept": "application/vnd.github.v3+json"}
    if token:
        headers["Authorization"] = f"token {token}"

    # ... [Internal helper closures fetch_branches and check_tree defined here] ...

    # Check if URL contains a specific branch/commit
    if len(path_parts) > 3 and path_parts[2] == "tree":

        def join_parts(i):
            return "/".join(path_parts[i:])

        branches = fetch_branches(owner, repo)
        branch_names = (branch.get("name") for branch in branches)

        # Fetching branches was not successful
        if len(branches) == 0:
            return None

        # Check branch name
        relevant_path = join_parts(3)

        # Find a match with relevant path and get the branch name
        filter_gen = (name for name in branch_names if relevant_path.startswith(name))
        ref = next(filter_gen, None)

        # If match is not found, check for is it a tree
        if ref is None:
            tree = path_parts[3]
            ref = tree if check_tree(owner, repo, tree) else None

        # If it is neither a tree nor a branch name
        if ref is None:
            emit_raw("ERROR", "The given path does not match with any branch and any tree in the repository.\nPlease verify the path is exists.")
            return None

        # Combine all parts after the ref as the path
        part_index = 5 if "/" in ref else 4
        specific_path = join_parts(part_index) if part_index < len(path_parts) else ""
    else:
        # Don't put the ref param in query
        # and let Github decide default branch
        ref = None
        specific_path = ""

In the REST API branch, the function parses the URL path to isolate owner and repo. When URLs contain /tree/, the subpath must be disambiguated between complex multi-slash branch names (e.g., feature/login), commit SHAs, or Git tree objects. The code queries fetch_branches() and searches for prefix matches against existing remote branch names. If no branch matches, it falls back to validating whether the path segment represents a valid Git tree commit SHA via check_tree(). Once the ref is identified, remaining path segments are combined to form the target root specific_path.

docs.title: Phase 4: Remote .gitignore Acquisition and Spec Compilation
docs.text:
Attempts to locate and retrieve the repository's root .gitignore file through the GitHub contents API before traversing code trees.

    # Dictionary to store path -> content mapping
    files = {}

    # --- Counters ---
    api_counters = {"processed": 0, "excluded": 0, "size_limit": 0, "non_text": 0, "entry": 0}
    api_skipped_size = []
    api_skipped_non_text = []

    # --- Try to fetch .gitignore ---
    gitignore_spec = None
    try:
        gi_url = f"https://api.github.com/repos/{owner}/{repo}/contents/.gitignore"
        gi_params = {"ref": ref} if ref is not None else {}
        gi_resp = requests.get(gi_url, headers=headers, params=gi_params, timeout=(10, 10))
        if gi_resp.status_code == 200:
            gi_data = gi_resp.json()
            if "content" in gi_data and gi_data.get("encoding") == "base64":
                gi_content = base64.b64decode(gi_data["content"]).decode("utf-8")
                gitignore_spec = pathspec.PathSpec.from_lines("gitwildmatch", gi_content.splitlines())
                emit("CRAWL_GITIGNORE_LOADED", path="repository (API)")
    except Exception:
        pass

Before initiating full directory crawling, the API engine performs a speculative HTTP GET request for /.gitignore pinned to the target ref. If the file exists and is encoded as base64, it decodes the payload to text and constructs a PathSpec matcher instance. If the file is missing (HTTP 404) or network errors occur, the exception is caught silently, leaving gitignore_spec as None so crawling can continue without .gitignore filtering.

docs.title: Phase 5: Recursive REST API Traversal and Content Extraction
docs.text:
Recursively crawls the repository tree via GitHub's /repos/{owner}/{repo}/contents/{path} endpoint, managing rate limit backoff and extracting raw file bodies.

    def fetch_contents(path):
        """Fetch contents of the repository at a specific path and commit"""
        url = f"https://api.github.com/repos/{owner}/{repo}/contents/{path}"
        params = {"ref": ref} if ref is not None else {}

        response = requests.get(url, headers=headers, params=params, timeout=(30, 30))

        if response.status_code in (403, 429) and "rate limit exceeded" in response.text.lower():
            if not token:
                raise Exception("GitHub API rate limit exceeded. Please provide a GitHub token using --token or GITHUB_TOKEN env var.")
            reset_time = int(response.headers.get("X-RateLimit-Reset", 0))
            wait_time = max(reset_time - time.time(), 0) + 1
            emit_raw("WARNING", f"Rate limit exceeded. Waiting for {wait_time:.0f} seconds...")
            time.sleep(wait_time)
            return fetch_contents(path)

        # ... [HTTP error status verification: 404, non-200] ...

        contents = response.json()

        # Handle both single file and directory responses
        if not isinstance(contents, list):
            contents = [contents]

        for item in contents:
            item_path = item["path"]

            # Calculate relative path if requested
            if use_relative_paths and specific_path:
                if item_path.startswith(specific_path):
                    rel_path = item_path[len(specific_path) :].lstrip("/")
                else:
                    rel_path = item_path
            else:
                rel_path = item_path

            if item["type"] == "file":
                api_counters["entry"] += 1
                entry_num = api_counters["entry"]

                if not should_include_file(rel_path, item["name"], gitignore_spec=gitignore_spec):
                    api_counters["excluded"] += 1
                    emit("CRAWL_FILE_EXCLUDED", num=entry_num, path=rel_path)
                    continue

                file_size = item.get("size", 0)
                if file_size > max_file_size:
                    api_counters["size_limit"] += 1
                    api_skipped_size.append(rel_path)
                    size_kb = file_size / 1024
                    emit("CRAWL_FILE_SIZE_LIMIT", num=entry_num, path=rel_path, size=f"{size_kb:.0f}")
                    continue

                if item.get("download_url"):
                    file_url = item["download_url"]
                    file_response = requests.get(file_url, headers=headers, timeout=(30, 30))
                    # ... [Content-Length validation and text assignment] ...
                else:
                    # Alternative method if download_url is not available (Base64 decoding)
                    # ...
            elif item["type"] == "dir":
                # ... [Directory exclusion evaluation and recursive call] ...
                fetch_contents(item_path)

The recursive fetch_contents helper queries the GitHub contents endpoint. If an HTTP 403 or 429 response indicates rate-limiting, the engine parses X-RateLimit-Reset, pauses execution with time.sleep(), and retries the request. When reading directory entries, it normalizes relative subpaths, verifies inclusion/exclusion criteria, checks the size metadata attribute against max_file_size, and retrieves file bodies. Content fetching prefers direct HTTP downloads from download_url, falling back to decoding Base64 JSON payloads from item["url"] when download_url is absent.

docs.title: Phase 6: Result Assembly and Summary Reporting
docs.text:
Aggregates crawl metrics across processed files, exclusions, size limit skips, and non-text omissions, emitting structured diagnostic summaries via output.py.

    # Start crawling from the specified path
    fetch_contents(specific_path)

    # --- Summary ---
    total_fetched = api_counters["processed"] + api_counters["excluded"] + api_counters["size_limit"] + api_counters["non_text"]
    emit("CRAWL_SUMMARY_HEADER")
    emit("CRAWL_SUMMARY_TOTAL", count=total_fetched)
    emit("CRAWL_SUMMARY_PROCESSED", count=api_counters["processed"])
    if api_counters["excluded"] > 0:
        emit("CRAWL_SUMMARY_EXCLUDED", count=api_counters["excluded"])
    if api_counters["size_limit"] > 0:
        emit("CRAWL_SUMMARY_SIZE_LIMIT", count=api_counters["size_limit"])
        for sf in api_skipped_size:
            emit("CRAWL_SUMMARY_ITEM", name=sf)
    if api_counters["non_text"] > 0:
        emit("CRAWL_SUMMARY_NON_TEXT", count=api_counters["non_text"])
        for sf in api_skipped_non_text:
            emit("CRAWL_SUMMARY_ITEM", name=sf)

    return {
        "files": files,
        "stats": {
            "downloaded_count": len(files),
            "skipped_count": 0,
            "skipped_files": [],
            "base_path": specific_path if use_relative_paths else None,
            "include_patterns": include_patterns,
            "exclude_patterns": exclude_patterns,
        },
    }

Upon completing the traversal, the function tallies cumulative statistics across all encountered items (processed, excluded, size_limit, non_text). It invokes standardized emit() telemetry events to print summary metrics and detailed lists of skipped files to the output console. Finally, it constructs and returns the structured dictionary containing the accumulated files map and metadata stats.

Example: 

# Extracted from utils/crawl_github_files.py (__main__ execution block)
repo_url = "https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/tree/6c38dc93f40a47f4d1350adca9ec0d72502e223f/pydantic"

result = crawl_github_files(
    repo_url,
    token=os.environ.get("GITHUB_TOKEN"),
    max_file_size=1 * 1024 * 1024,  # 1 MB in bytes
    use_relative_paths=True,        # Enable relative paths
    include_patterns={"*.py", "*.md"}, # Include Python and Markdown files
)

files = result["files"]
stats = result["stats"]

docs.title: should_include_file()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private (Nested Helper inside crawl_github_files) Signature: def should_include_file(file_path: str, file_name: str, gitignore_spec: pathspec.PathSpec | None = None) -> bool:

Description: Evaluates whether an individual file should be ingested based on glob inclusion patterns, compiled .gitignore rules, and exclusion patterns. Inclusion rules are evaluated against the basename (file_name), whereas exclusion and .gitignore rules are evaluated against the repository-relative path (file_path).

Parameters: * file_path (str): Relative path of the candidate file within the repository. * file_name (str): Basename (filename only) of the candidate file. * gitignore_spec (pathspec.PathSpec | None, optional): Compiled PathSpec matcher instance derived from the repository's .gitignore. Defaults to None.

Returns: * bool: True if the file satisfies all inclusion criteria and violates no exclusion or gitignore rules; False otherwise.

Example: 

# Extracted from utils/crawl_github_files.py (inside crawl_github_files)
def should_include_file(file_path: str, file_name: str, gitignore_spec=None) -> bool:
    """Determine if a file should be included based on patterns"""
    # If no include patterns are specified, include all files
    if not include_patterns:
        include_file = True
    else:
        # Check if file matches any include pattern
        include_file = any(fnmatch.fnmatch(file_name, pattern) for pattern in include_patterns)

    # Check gitignore if provided
    if include_file and gitignore_spec and gitignore_spec.match_file(file_path):
        return False

    # If exclude patterns are specified, check if file should be excluded
    if exclude_patterns and include_file:
        # Exclude if file matches any exclude pattern
        exclude_file = any(fnmatch.fnmatch(file_path, pattern) for pattern in exclude_patterns)
        return not exclude_file

    return include_file

The helper enforces precedence rules: if include_patterns is defined, the filename must match at least one pattern. Next, if gitignore_spec is active and matches file_path, the file is rejected immediately. Finally, if exclude_patterns are provided and match file_path, the file is excluded.

docs.title: fetch_branches()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private (Nested Helper inside crawl_github_files) Signature: def fetch_branches(owner: str, repo: str) -> list[dict]:

Description: Queries the GitHub REST API endpoint /repos/{owner}/{repo}/branches to obtain a list of all existing branches for the target repository. Used to resolve ambiguous URL path segments that may refer to multi-part branch names.

Parameters: * owner (str): GitHub repository owner (organization or username). * repo (str): GitHub repository name.

Returns: * list[dict]: List of branch representation dictionaries returned by the GitHub API. Returns an empty list [] if an error occurs or the repository is inaccessible.

Raises: * Exception: If unauthenticated GitHub API rate limits (HTTP 403 or 429) are encountered without an access token.

Example: 

# Extracted from utils/crawl_github_files.py (inside crawl_github_files)
def fetch_branches(owner: str, repo: str):
    """Get branches of the repository"""

    url = f"https://api.github.com/repos/{owner}/{repo}/branches"
    response = requests.get(url, headers=headers, timeout=(30, 30))

    if response.status_code in (403, 429) and not token:
        raise Exception("GitHub API rate limit exceeded. Please provide a GitHub token using --token or GITHUB_TOKEN env var.")

    if response.status_code == 404:
        if not token:
            emit_raw(
                "ERROR",
                "Error 404: Repository not found or is private.\n"
                "If this is a private repository, please provide a valid GitHub token via the 'token' argument or set the GITHUB_TOKEN environment variable.",
            )
        else:
            emit_raw(
                "ERROR",
                "Error 404: Repository not found or insufficient permissions with the provided token.\n"
                "Please verify the repository exists and the token has access to this repository.",
            )
        return []

    if response.status_code != 200:
        emit_raw("ERROR", f"Error fetching the branches of {owner}/{repo}: {response.status_code} - {response.text}")
        return []

    return response.json()

The function executes a synchronized HTTP GET request with a 30-second connect/read timeout. It intercepts HTTP 403 and 429 status codes, raising a fatal exception if unauthenticated, or reporting granular 404 diagnostics differentiating between missing public repositories and private repositories requiring a GitHub PAT.

docs.title: check_tree()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private (Nested Helper inside crawl_github_files) Signature: def check_tree(owner: str, repo: str, tree: str) -> bool:

Description: Checks whether a specified Git tree object or commit SHA exists in the remote GitHub repository by issuing a HEAD/GET request to /repos/{owner}/{repo}/git/trees/{tree}.

Parameters: * owner (str): GitHub repository owner. * repo (str): GitHub repository name. * tree (str): Commit SHA, tree SHA, or tag reference to validate.

Returns: * bool: True if the tree object exists (HTTP status 200); False otherwise.

Raises: * Exception: If unauthenticated GitHub API rate limits are encountered.

Example: 

# Extracted from utils/crawl_github_files.py (inside crawl_github_files)
def check_tree(owner: str, repo: str, tree: str):
    """Check the repository has the given tree"""

    url = f"https://api.github.com/repos/{owner}/{repo}/git/trees/{tree}"
    response = requests.get(url, headers=headers, timeout=(30, 30))

    if response.status_code in (403, 429) and not token:
        raise Exception("GitHub API rate limit exceeded. Please provide a GitHub token using --token or GITHUB_TOKEN env var.")

    return response.status_code == 200

check_tree validates commit SHAs when URL path parsing cannot match an explicit branch name from fetch_branches(). If the tree query returns HTTP 200, the commit SHA is confirmed as valid, allowing the crawler to anchor recursive contents requests to that specific tree ref.

docs.title: fetch_contents()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private (Nested Helper inside crawl_github_files) Signature: def fetch_contents(path: str) -> None:

Description: Recursively traverses and downloads files from the GitHub repository contents endpoint. Handles directory recursion, exclusion pruning, rate limit sleep-and-retry logic, file size checking, download URL streaming, and Base64 content decoding. Populates the outer files dictionary by side effect.

Parameters: * path (str): Subdirectory path within the repository to fetch. Passes an empty string "" to begin traversal at the root.

Returns: * None: Populates the outer scope files dictionary and increments api_counters directly.

Raises: * Exception: If an unauthenticated rate limit error is encountered.

Example: 

# Extracted from utils/crawl_github_files.py (inside crawl_github_files)
def fetch_contents(path):
    """Fetch contents of the repository at a specific path and commit"""
    url = f"https://api.github.com/repos/{owner}/{repo}/contents/{path}"
    params = {"ref": ref} if ref is not None else {}

    response = requests.get(url, headers=headers, params=params, timeout=(30, 30))

    if response.status_code in (403, 429) and "rate limit exceeded" in response.text.lower():
        if not token:
            raise Exception("GitHub API rate limit exceeded. Please provide a GitHub token using --token or GITHUB_TOKEN env var.")
        reset_time = int(response.headers.get("X-RateLimit-Reset", 0))
        wait_time = max(reset_time - time.time(), 0) + 1
        emit_raw("WARNING", f"Rate limit exceeded. Waiting for {wait_time:.0f} seconds...")
        time.sleep(wait_time)
        return fetch_contents(path)

    if response.status_code == 404:
        # ... [Handle 404 error formatting] ...
        return None

    if response.status_code != 200:
        emit_raw("ERROR", f"Error fetching {path}: {response.status_code} - {response.text}")
        return None

    contents = response.json()
    if not isinstance(contents, list):
        contents = [contents]

    for item in contents:
        # ... [Process file downloads and directory recursion] ...
        pass
    return None

fetch_contents manages directory recursion over the GitHub API. When encountering a directory (item["type"] == "dir"), it tests the directory against .gitignore and glob exclusion rules before making recursive calls. For files (item["type"] == "file"), it verifies size limits against item["size"], issues HTTP GET requests to download_url, checks the resulting Content-Length header, and stores decoded UTF-8 file content in the outer files mapping.

docs.title: Return Schema: Repository Crawl Result
docs.text:
Both the SSH clone and REST API engines return a dictionary conforming to the structural schema below.

{
    "files": {
        "src/main.py": "import os\n...",
        "README.md": "# Project\n..."
    },
    "stats": {
        "downloaded_count": 2,
        "skipped_count": 0,
        "skipped_files": [],
        "base_path": "src",
        "include_patterns": {"*.py", "*.md"},
        "exclude_patterns": None,
        "source": "ssh_clone"  # Present only in SSH mode
    }
}

docs.title: Fields: Top-Level Mapping
docs.text: Field Type Description files dict[str, str] Mapping of file paths (relative to repository root or base_path) to UTF-8 file contents. stats dict[str, Any] Execution metadata, filter criteria, and transfer statistics.

docs.title: Fields: stats Sub-Dictionary
docs.text: Field Type Description downloaded_count int Total number of valid text files successfully ingested into files. skipped_count int Reserved counter for skipped files (defaults to 0). skipped_files list[str] Reserved list for skipped file paths (defaults to []). base_path str | None Base path offset used if use_relative_paths=True; otherwise None. include_patterns set[str] | None Glob pattern set applied for file inclusion. exclude_patterns set[str] | None Glob pattern set applied for file/directory exclusion. source str (Optional) Identifies the ingestion mechanism. Set to "ssh_clone" when the SSH engine is used.

docs.title: Internal State: api_counters Tracking Schema
docs.text:
Used internally by the REST API crawler to aggregate telemetry across traversal steps.

Field Type Description processed int Count of successfully ingested and decoded text files. excluded int Count of files and directories skipped due to .gitignore or exclusion patterns. size_limit int Count of files skipped due to exceeding max_file_size. non_text int Count of files skipped due to binary encoding, decoding failures, or HTTP download errors. entry int Total count of all evaluated filesystem entries (files and directories).

docs.title: Error Handling
docs.text: utils/crawl_github_files.py handles diverse network, transport, filesystem, and rate limit errors:

docs.title: 1. GitHub API Rate Limiting (HTTP 403 / 429)
docs.text:
• Unauthenticated Requests: If no token is supplied and GitHub returns an HTTP 403 or 429 containing "rate limit exceeded", execution raises an immediate Exception notifying the user that an API token is required.
  • Authenticated Requests: If an authenticated session hits a rate limit, the engine extracts the X-RateLimit-Reset Unix epoch timestamp, calculates the required sleep duration (reset_time - time.time() + 1), logs a warning event via emit_raw("WARNING", ...), sleeps using time.sleep(), and retries the request automatically.

docs.title: 2. HTTP 404 Repository and Ref Resolution Diagnostics
docs.text: The engine differentiates 404 error causes based on authentication context and URL paths: * Private or Missing Repositories: Emits a targeted advisory explaining that the repository may be private (requiring a token via GITHUB_TOKEN) or does not exist. * Branch Name Heuristics: If querying root paths on default branches fails, it alerts the user to check if the repository uses an alternative default branch (such as master instead of main). * Invalid Trees: If URL path segments after /tree/ do not match any branch from /branches or commit tree from /git/trees/{tree}, it halts execution and returns None.

docs.title: 3. File Size and Memory Protection
docs.text:
• Files are validated against max_file_size at three distinct checkpoints:
  • REST API file metadata (item.get("size", 0)).
  • HTTP download streaming headers (Content-Length).
  • Base64 payload length heuristics (len(content) * 0.75).
  • Files exceeding the threshold increment count_size_limit / api_counters["size_limit"], are logged to the skipped lists, and trigger a CRAWL_FILE_SIZE_LIMIT event without downloading the full payload.

docs.title: 4. Binary and Non-Text Ingestion Failures
docs.text:
• SSH Engine: Catches UnicodeDecodeError and ValueError when opening files with utf-8-sig, logging them as non-text via CRAWL_FILE_NOT_TEXT.
  • API Engine: Validates Base64 decoding and HTTP response statuses, catching parsing errors and emitting CRAWL_FILE_HTTP_ERROR or CRAWL_FILE_UNEXPECTED.

  • exclude_patterns.py — Defines default exclusion pattern lists passed into crawl_github_files().
  • output.py — Telemetry subsystem consumed by this module for emit(), emit_raw(), and localized string retrieval via get().
  • call_llm.py — Model execution engine that processes the ingested file dictionary.
  • nodes.py — Implements crawl_repo_node(), which directly invokes crawl_github_files() during workflow graph execution.

docs.title: utils.crawl_local_files
docs.text:
utils/crawl_local_files.py

As the local filesystem counterpart to utils.crawl_github_files, this module provides directory traversal, file filtering, and content extraction capabilities for repositories stored locally on disk. It produces an output dictionary structure matching the remote GitHub crawler ({"files": {filepath: content}}), ensuring seamless interoperability across the ingestion pipeline.

docs.title: Technical Overview
docs.text: The module traverses local directories using a single-pass os.walk strategy with in-place directory pruning. During traversal, it respects git-ignore rules, glob inclusion/exclusion patterns, and file size limits, while safely extracting UTF-8 text content and discarding binary files.

docs.title: Key Capabilities
docs.text:
1. .gitignore Integration: Automatically detects and compiles repository-level .gitignore files using pathspec (with gitwildmatch syntax) to prune ignored paths before traversal.
  2. Directory Pruning: Mutates dirs in-place during os.walk execution to prevent traversing into excluded directory trees (e.g., .git, virtual environments, or node_modules).
  3. Filtering Pipeline: Applies exclusion patterns, inclusion filters, and size constraints sequentially to minimize unnecessary I/O operations.
  4. Encoding & Binary Safety: Reads file contents using utf-8-sig to automatically strip byte-order marks (BOM) while capturing UnicodeDecodeError and general exceptions to skip binary assets.
  5. ANSI Console Reporting: Emits formatted, color-coded logging for each encountered item and outputs a structured summary table at the end of the crawl process.

docs.title: crawl_local_files()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def crawl_local_files(directory, include_patterns=None, exclude_patterns=None, max_file_size=None, use_relative_paths=True)

Description: Crawls a local directory path, applying gitignore specifications, user-defined exclusion patterns, inclusion patterns, and file size restrictions. Files that pass all filter stages are read from disk using the utf-8-sig encoding format and stored in an internal dictionary indexed by their path.

Parameters: * directory (str): Target root filesystem path to crawl. * include_patterns (set | None): Optional set of glob patterns indicating which files should be included (e.g., {"*.py", "*.js"}). If provided, any file not matching at least one pattern is excluded. * exclude_patterns (set | None): Optional set of glob patterns indicating files or directories to skip (e.g., {"tests/*", "*.pyc"}). * max_file_size (int | None): Maximum allowed file size in bytes. Larger files are bypassed. * use_relative_paths (bool): If True, keys in the returned dictionary are relative to directory. If False, absolute/resolved filesystem paths are retained. Default is True.

Returns: * dict: A dictionary containing a single key "files", mapping string file paths to their read string contents: 

{"files": {filepath: content}}

Raises: * ValueError: Raised immediately if directory does not exist or is not recognized as a directory by os.path.isdir.

Implementation Logic:

    if not os.path.isdir(directory):
        raise ValueError(f"Directory does not exist: {directory}")

    files_dict = {}

    # --- ANSI colors ---
    C_GREEN = "\033[92m"
    C_GRAY = "\033[90m"
    C_RED = "\033[91m"
    C_RESET = "\033[0m"

    # --- Counters ---
    entry_num = 0
    count_processed = 0
    count_excluded = 0
    count_size_limit = 0
    count_non_text = 0
    skipped_size_limit = []
    skipped_non_text = []

    # --- Load .gitignore ---
    gitignore_path = os.path.join(directory, ".gitignore")
    gitignore_spec = None
    if os.path.exists(gitignore_path):
        try:
            with open(gitignore_path, encoding="utf-8-sig") as f:
                gitignore_patterns = f.readlines()
            gitignore_spec = pathspec.PathSpec.from_lines("gitwildmatch", gitignore_patterns)
            print(f"Loaded .gitignore patterns from {gitignore_path}")
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"Warning: Could not read or parse .gitignore file {gitignore_path}: {e}")
    # ...

The function initiates by validating the directory and preparing console logging tracking variables. It looks for a top-level .gitignore file within the specified directory. When found, it parses the ignore lines into a pathspec.PathSpec object using the gitwildmatch standard. Parsing errors are caught gracefully with a warning output, allowing the crawl to proceed even if .gitignore syntax is invalid or unreadable.

    # ...
    # --- Single-pass: walk, filter, and process inline ---
    for root, dirs, files in os.walk(directory):
        # --- Directory filtering ---
        excluded_dirs = set()
        for d in sorted(dirs):
            dirpath_rel = os.path.relpath(os.path.join(root, d), directory)

            reason = None
            if gitignore_spec and gitignore_spec.match_file(dirpath_rel):
                reason = "excluded (.gitignore)"
            elif exclude_patterns:
                for pattern in exclude_patterns:
                    dir_pattern = pattern.removesuffix("/*")
                    if fnmatch.fnmatch(dirpath_rel, dir_pattern) or fnmatch.fnmatch(d, dir_pattern):
                        reason = "excluded"
                        break

            if reason:
                excluded_dirs.add(d)
                entry_num += 1
                count_excluded += 1
                print(f"{C_GRAY}  [{entry_num}] {dirpath_rel}/ [{reason}]{C_RESET}")

        for d in dirs.copy():
            if d in excluded_dirs:
                dirs.remove(d)

        # Sort remaining dirs for consistent traversal order
        dirs.sort()
        # ...

For directory pruning, os.walk is traversed top-down. Candidate directory names in dirs are evaluated against both the parsed .gitignore pattern specification and the caller-provided exclude_patterns (handling patterns with or without trailing /*). Any directory matching an exclusion rule is collected in excluded_dirs and purged in-place from dirs via dirs.remove(d). This prevents os.walk from descending into unnecessary subtrees, significantly reducing crawl time on large repositories. Remaining directories are sorted in-place to guarantee deterministic traversal order.

        # ...
        # --- File processing (inline, sorted) ---
        for filename in sorted(files):
            filepath = os.path.join(root, filename)
            relpath = os.path.relpath(filepath, directory) if use_relative_paths else filepath
            entry_num += 1

            # Check gitignore
            if gitignore_spec and gitignore_spec.match_file(relpath):
                count_excluded += 1
                print(f"{C_GRAY}  [{entry_num}] {relpath} [excluded (.gitignore)]{C_RESET}")
                continue

            # Check exclude patterns
            excluded = False
            if exclude_patterns:
                for pattern in exclude_patterns:
                    if fnmatch.fnmatch(relpath, pattern):
                        excluded = True
                        break
            if excluded:
                count_excluded += 1
                print(f"{C_GRAY}  [{entry_num}] {relpath} [excluded]{C_RESET}")
                continue

            # Check include patterns
            if include_patterns:
                matched = False
                for pattern in include_patterns:
                    if fnmatch.fnmatch(relpath, pattern):
                        matched = True
                        break
                if not matched:
                    count_excluded += 1
                    print(f"{C_GRAY}  [{entry_num}] {relpath} [excluded (not in include list)]{C_RESET}")
                    continue

            # Check size limit
            if max_file_size and os.path.getsize(filepath) > max_file_size:
                count_size_limit += 1
                skipped_size_limit.append(relpath)
                size_kb = os.path.getsize(filepath) / 1024
                print(f"{C_RED}  [{entry_num}] {relpath} [size limit: {size_kb:.0f}KB]{C_RESET}")
                continue

            # Try to read as text
            try:
                with open(filepath, encoding="utf-8-sig") as f:
                    content = f.read()
                files_dict[relpath] = content
                count_processed += 1
                print(f"{C_GREEN}  [{entry_num}] {relpath} [processed]{C_RESET}")
            except (UnicodeDecodeError, ValueError):
                count_non_text += 1
                skipped_non_text.append(relpath)
                print(f"{C_RED}  [{entry_num}] {relpath} [cannot process: not a text file]{C_RESET}")
            except Exception as e:
                count_non_text += 1
                skipped_non_text.append(relpath)
                print(f"{C_RED}  [{entry_num}] {relpath} [cannot process: {e}]{C_RESET}")
    # ...

Files within each directory are evaluated in sorted order. For each candidate file: 1. It is matched against .gitignore using pathspec.match_file(). 2. It is checked against caller-provided exclude_patterns using fnmatch.fnmatch(). 3. If include_patterns is provided, the path must match at least one inclusion pattern; otherwise, it is skipped. 4. If max_file_size is specified and the file's disk size exceeds this threshold, the file is skipped and logged with its size in kilobytes. 5. If all checks pass, the file is opened with utf-8-sig encoding. If the file is binary or has an incompatible encoding, a UnicodeDecodeError or ValueError is caught, and the path is cataloged in skipped_non_text. Any other filesystem I/O exceptions are caught and reported as non-text errors without crashing the crawler.

    # ...
    # --- Summary ---
    total_fetched = count_processed + count_excluded + count_size_limit + count_non_text
    print("\n--- Crawl Summary ---")
    print(f"  Total found : {total_fetched}")
    print(f"{C_GREEN}  Processed   : {count_processed}{C_RESET}")
    if count_excluded > 0:
        print(f"{C_GRAY}  Excluded    : {count_excluded}{C_RESET}")
    if count_size_limit > 0:
        print(f"{C_RED}  Size limit  : {count_size_limit}{C_RESET}")
        for f in skipped_size_limit:
            print(f"{C_RED}    - {f}{C_RESET}")
    if count_non_text > 0:
        print(f"{C_RED}  Non-text    : {count_non_text}{C_RESET}")
        for f in skipped_non_text:
            print(f"{C_RED}    - {f}{C_RESET}")
    print("---------------------")

    return {"files": files_dict}

Once os.walk finishes traversing the target directory tree, crawl_local_files aggregates statistics for total entries found, successfully processed files, excluded items, files exceeding the size threshold, and non-text/unreadable files. It prints this detailed breakdown to standard output and returns the final dictionary.

Usage Example:

# Extract from utils/crawl_local_files.py (__main__ execution block)
if __name__ == "__main__":
    print("--- Crawling parent directory ('..') ---")
    files_data = crawl_local_files(
        "..",
        exclude_patterns={
            "*.pyc",
            "__pycache__/*",
            ".venv/*",
            ".git/*",
            "docs/*",
            "output/*",
        },
    )
    print(f"Found {len(files_data['files'])} files:")
    for path in files_data["files"]:
        print(f"  {path}")

docs.title: Technical Overview
docs.text:
While crawl_github_files.py handles remote GitHub repository extraction across REST API endpoints and temporary clone sandboxes, utils/crawl_local_files.py implements the local filesystem ingestion engine for the Codebase-Knowledge-Builder system. Its primary responsibility is to recursively traverse on-disk directory trees, evaluate exclusion and inclusion rules, compile and apply hierarchical .gitignore path specifications, filter out non-text binaries or oversized files, and assemble the resulting source code into a standardized in-memory dictionary for downstream processing.

The module operates as a single-pass filesystem crawler built on Python's standard os.walk() generator. Rather than performing an unconstrained scan and filtering results post-traversal, crawl_local_files.py performs in-place mutation of directory lists during traversal (dirs[:]). This early-pruning strategy avoids descending into ignored subtrees such as .git, virtual environments, build directories, or nested ignore targets. It manages hierarchical .gitignore files dynamically, parsing nested .gitignore configurations as new directory scopes are encountered during traversal and scoping rule evaluations relative to the directory containing the respective ignore file.

In addition to Git-compliant ignore rules powered by the pathspec library, the crawler evaluates glob-based include and exclude pattern sets via fnmatch. Files that survive the multi-tier filtering pipeline undergo size checks against a configurable byte threshold before safe UTF-8-SIG reading. Binary files, decode failures, and I/O errors are trapped defensively and recorded into telemetry streams via utils.output.emit(). The module produces an identical dictionary schema to its remote counterpart, enabling seamless interchangeability within the workflow execution graph in nodes.py.

docs.title: crawl_local_files()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def crawl_local_files(directory, include_patterns=None, exclude_patterns=None, max_file_size=None, use_relative_paths=True)

Description: Traverses a local filesystem directory recursively, applying layered exclusion patterns, inclusion patterns, hierarchical .gitignore rules, file size limits, and binary decoding filters. Operates in a single pass using os.walk() with in-place directory mutation for performance. Files successfully parsed as UTF-8 text are captured in a mapping of normalized filepaths to their text content. Traversal progress and summary statistics are published through the utils.output messaging system.

docs.title: Phase 1: Directory Validation and Metric Initialization
docs.text:
if not os.path.isdir(directory):
        raise ValueError(f"Directory does not exist: {directory}")

    files_dict = {}

    # --- Counters ---
    entry_num = 0
    count_processed = 0
    count_excluded = 0
    count_size_limit = 0
    count_non_text = 0
    skipped_size_limit = []
    skipped_non_text = []

    # --- Gitignore specs: {abs_dir_path: pathspec} ---
    gitignore_specs = {}
    root_gi_path = os.path.join(directory, ".gitignore")
    if os.path.exists(root_gi_path):
        spec = _load_gitignore(root_gi_path)
        if spec:
            gitignore_specs[os.path.abspath(directory)] = spec
            emit("CRAWL_GITIGNORE_LOADED", path=root_gi_path)

    # Translated reason strings (looked up once)
    reason_excluded = get("CRAWL_REASON_EXCLUDED")
    reason_gitignore = get("CRAWL_REASON_GITIGNORE")
The function verifies that the target directory exists on the local filesystem and is a directory; otherwise, it raises a ValueError. It initializes the output dictionary files_dict alongside traversal counters for telemetry. The root .gitignore file (if present) is loaded into the gitignore_specs dictionary, keyed by the absolute path of the root directory. Localized reason strings are retrieved upfront from output.py via get() to avoid repeated dictionary lookups during the traversal loop.

docs.title: Phase 2: Traversal Setup and Nested Gitignore Discovery
docs.text:
# --- Single-pass: walk, filter, and process inline ---
    for root, dirs, files in os.walk(directory):
        abs_root = os.path.abspath(root)

        # Check for nested .gitignore in current directory (skip root, already loaded)
        if abs_root != os.path.abspath(directory):
            nested_gi = os.path.join(root, ".gitignore")
            if os.path.exists(nested_gi):
                spec = _load_gitignore(nested_gi)
                if spec:
                    gitignore_specs[abs_root] = spec
The crawler initiates an os.walk() traversal starting at the root directory. At each directory level (root), it resolves the absolute path abs_root and checks for a nested .gitignore file. If a nested ignore file is discovered outside the root directory, it is compiled into a pathspec.PathSpec via _load_gitignore() and appended to the gitignore_specs mapping, extending path matching rules to all subpaths under that specific directory tree.

docs.title: Phase 3: Directory Pruning and Pattern Exclusion
docs.text:
# --- Directory filtering ---
        excluded_dirs = set()
        for d in sorted(dirs):
            abs_d = os.path.join(abs_root, d)
            dirpath_rel = os.path.relpath(abs_d, directory)

            reason = None
            if _matches_any_gitignore(gitignore_specs, abs_d, is_dir=True):
                reason = reason_gitignore
            elif exclude_patterns:
                for pattern in exclude_patterns:
                    dir_pattern = pattern.removesuffix("/*")
                    if fnmatch.fnmatch(dirpath_rel, dir_pattern) or fnmatch.fnmatch(d, dir_pattern):
                        reason = reason_excluded
                        break

            if reason:
                excluded_dirs.add(d)
                entry_num += 1
                count_excluded += 1
                emit("CRAWL_DIR_EXCLUDED", num=entry_num, path=dirpath_rel, reason=reason)

        for d in dirs.copy():
            if d in excluded_dirs:
                dirs.remove(d)

        # Sort remaining dirs for consistent traversal order
        dirs.sort()
Directory entries in dirs are sorted and evaluated against both the compiled gitignore_specs (with is_dir=True) and explicit exclude_patterns. For exclude patterns, trailing /* wildcards are stripped using .removesuffix("/*") to allow directory-level matches on both full relative paths (dirpath_rel) and local folder names (d). When a directory matches an exclusion rule, it is added to excluded_dirs, its exclusion is emitted to telemetry, and it is removed directly from dirs using dirs.remove(d). Mutating dirs in place instructs os.walk() not to descend into those subtrees. Remaining valid directories are sorted to enforce deterministic traversal order.

docs.title: Phase 4: Multi-Stage File Filtering Cascade
docs.text:
# --- File processing (inline, sorted) ---
        for filename in sorted(files):
            filepath = os.path.join(root, filename)
            abs_filepath = os.path.abspath(filepath)
            relpath = os.path.relpath(filepath, directory) if use_relative_paths else filepath
            entry_num += 1

            # Check gitignore (all levels)
            if _matches_any_gitignore(gitignore_specs, abs_filepath):
                count_excluded += 1
                emit("CRAWL_FILE_GITIGNORE", num=entry_num, path=relpath)
                continue

            # Check exclude patterns
            excluded = False
            if exclude_patterns:
                for pattern in exclude_patterns:
                    if fnmatch.fnmatch(relpath, pattern):
                        excluded = True
                        break
            if excluded:
                count_excluded += 1
                emit("CRAWL_FILE_EXCLUDED", num=entry_num, path=relpath)
                continue

            # Check include patterns
            if include_patterns:
                matched = False
                for pattern in include_patterns:
                    if fnmatch.fnmatch(relpath, pattern):
                        matched = True
                        break
                if not matched:
                    count_excluded += 1
                    emit("CRAWL_FILE_NOT_INCLUDED", num=entry_num, path=relpath)
                    continue
For each file in the current directory (sorted alphabetically), the crawler determines the relative path relpath and advances the global entry_num. The file is passed through a three-stage sequential filter gate: 1. Gitignore Evaluation: Evaluated against all registered .gitignore specs via _matches_any_gitignore(). 2. Exclude Patterns: Evaluated against exclude_patterns using fnmatch.fnmatch() against relpath. 3. Include Patterns: If include_patterns is provided, relpath must match at least one pattern; otherwise, it is rejected.

Rejection at any stage emits a corresponding telemetry event (CRAWL_FILE_GITIGNORE, CRAWL_FILE_EXCLUDED, or CRAWL_FILE_NOT_INCLUDED), increments count_excluded, and skips further processing for that file.

docs.title: Phase 5: File Size Check and Safe Text Ingestion
docs.text:
# Check size limit
            if max_file_size and os.path.getsize(filepath) > max_file_size:
                count_size_limit += 1
                skipped_size_limit.append(relpath)
                size_kb = os.path.getsize(filepath) / 1024
                emit("CRAWL_FILE_SIZE_LIMIT", num=entry_num, path=relpath, size=f"{size_kb:.0f}")
                continue

            # Try to read as text
            try:
                with open(filepath, encoding="utf-8-sig") as f:
                    content = f.read()
                files_dict[relpath] = content
                count_processed += 1
                emit("CRAWL_FILE_PROCESSED", num=entry_num, path=relpath)
            except (UnicodeDecodeError, ValueError):
                count_non_text += 1
                skipped_non_text.append(relpath)
                emit("CRAWL_FILE_NOT_TEXT", num=entry_num, path=relpath)
            except Exception as e:
                count_non_text += 1
                skipped_non_text.append(relpath)
                emit("CRAWL_FILE_ERROR", num=entry_num, path=relpath, error=e)
Files passing pattern filters are checked against max_file_size. If the file size on disk exceeds this limit, count_size_limit is incremented, the relative path is added to skipped_size_limit, and CRAWL_FILE_SIZE_LIMIT is emitted. Otherwise, the crawler attempts to read the file using utf-8-sig encoding (which transparently strips UTF-8 Byte Order Marks). If successful, the content is stored in files_dict[relpath], count_processed is incremented, and CRAWL_FILE_PROCESSED is emitted. Non-text binaries triggering UnicodeDecodeError or ValueError, as well as unexpected filesystem read errors, are caught defensively, tracked in skipped_non_text, and reported via telemetry.

docs.title: Phase 6: Telemetry Reporting and Result Packaging
docs.text:
# --- Summary ---
    total_fetched = count_processed + count_excluded + count_size_limit + count_non_text
    emit("CRAWL_SUMMARY_HEADER")
    emit("CRAWL_SUMMARY_TOTAL", count=total_fetched)
    emit("CRAWL_SUMMARY_PROCESSED", count=count_processed)
    if count_excluded > 0:
        emit("CRAWL_SUMMARY_EXCLUDED", count=count_excluded)
    if count_size_limit > 0:
        emit("CRAWL_SUMMARY_SIZE_LIMIT", count=count_size_limit)
        for f in skipped_size_limit:
            emit("CRAWL_SUMMARY_ITEM", name=f)
    if count_non_text > 0:
        emit("CRAWL_SUMMARY_NON_TEXT", count=count_non_text)
        for f in skipped_non_text:
            emit("CRAWL_SUMMARY_ITEM", name=f)

    return {"files": files_dict}
After completing directory traversal, the function computes total_fetched as the sum of all processed, excluded, size-limited, and non-text entries. It emits a formatted summary breakdown using output.py messages, listing individual filenames for skipped oversized and binary files when applicable. Finally, it packages the processed file mapping into a dictionary conforming to the standard repository schema {"files": files_dict} and returns it to the caller.

Parameters: * directory (str): Absolute or relative filesystem path to the root target directory to crawl. * include_patterns (set | None): Optional set of glob patterns (e.g., {"*.py", "*.ts"}). If specified, only files matching at least one pattern are ingested. * exclude_patterns (set | None): Optional set of glob patterns to exclude (e.g., {"tests/*", "*.lock"}). Takes precedence over include_patterns. * max_file_size (int | None): Maximum allowable file size in bytes. Files exceeding this threshold are skipped. * use_relative_paths (bool): Whether dictionary keys should be formatted relative to directory (True, default) or preserved as full filesystem paths (False).

Returns: * dict: A dictionary containing the single key "files", mapped to an inner dictionary {filepath: content} of relative filepaths to UTF-8 decoded text contents.

Raises: * ValueError: If directory does not exist or is not a valid directory on the local filesystem.

Example: 

# Standalone usage example extracted from utils/crawl_local_files.py (__main__ block)
if __name__ == "__main__":
    print("--- Crawling parent directory ('..') ---")
    files_data = crawl_local_files(
        "..",
        exclude_patterns={
            "*.pyc",
            "__pycache__/*",
            ".venv/*",
            ".git/*",
            "docs/*",
            "output/*",
        },
    )
    print(f"Found {len(files_data['files'])} files:")
    for path in files_data["files"]:
        print(f"  {path}")

docs.title: _load_gitignore()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _load_gitignore(gitignore_path) -> pathspec.PathSpec | None:

Description: Attempts to open and parse a .gitignore file from disk using utf-8-sig encoding, compiling its lines into a pathspec.PathSpec object using the "gitwildmatch" pattern syntax. If the file cannot be opened, is unreadable, or contains invalid pattern syntax, the function traps all exceptions and safely returns None.

Implementation: 

def _load_gitignore(gitignore_path):
    """Load a .gitignore file and return a PathSpec, or None on failure."""
    try:
        with open(gitignore_path, encoding="utf-8-sig") as f:
            return pathspec.PathSpec.from_lines("gitwildmatch", f.readlines())
    except Exception:
        return None
This helper encapsulates .gitignore parsing with defensive error handling. By utilizing utf-8-sig, it handles files with or without UTF-8 BOM headers. The compiled PathSpec object adheres strictly to Git wildmatch rules (such as double-asterisk recursive globs and leading slash anchors). If an I/O error or syntax error occurs, the crawler logs no failure and continues traversal without applying the broken ignore specification.

Parameters: * gitignore_path (str): Filesystem path to the .gitignore file to read and compile.

Returns: * pathspec.PathSpec | None: A compiled PathSpec instance if parsing succeeded, or None if an exception occurred.

Example: 

# Internal call site within crawl_local_files()
root_gi_path = os.path.join(directory, ".gitignore")
if os.path.exists(root_gi_path):
    spec = _load_gitignore(root_gi_path)
    if spec:
        gitignore_specs[os.path.abspath(directory)] = spec
        emit("CRAWL_GITIGNORE_LOADED", path=root_gi_path)

docs.title: _matches_any_gitignore()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _matches_any_gitignore(gitignore_specs, abs_path, is_dir=False) -> bool:

Description: Evaluates whether a given absolute filesystem path matches any loaded .gitignore specification in gitignore_specs. It computes the path relative to each .gitignore's containing directory scope, normalizes backslashes to forward slashes for cross-platform compatibility, appends a trailing slash for directories, and checks the compiled PathSpec matcher.

Implementation: 

def _matches_any_gitignore(gitignore_specs, abs_path, is_dir=False):
    """Check if a path matches ANY loaded .gitignore spec.

    Each spec is checked with the path relative to its own .gitignore directory.
    For directories, a trailing '/' is appended for proper gitignore matching.

    Args:
        gitignore_specs: dict of {abs_dir_path: pathspec.PathSpec}
        abs_path: absolute path of the file or directory to check
        is_dir: True if checking a directory
    Returns:
        True if the path matches any gitignore rule
    """
    for gi_dir, spec in gitignore_specs.items():
        rel = os.path.relpath(abs_path, gi_dir)
        # Skip if the path is not under this gitignore's scope
        if rel.startswith(".."):
            continue
        match_path = rel.replace("\\", "/")
        if is_dir:
            match_path = match_path.rstrip("/") + "/"
        if spec.match_file(match_path):
            return True
    return False
This function resolves path scoping for hierarchical .gitignore configurations. It iterates through all registered ignore specifications in gitignore_specs. If os.path.relpath(abs_path, gi_dir) starts with .., the path lies outside the directory scope of that particular .gitignore and is skipped. For paths within scope, Windows backslashes (\) are converted to standard Git forward slashes (/). If is_dir=True, a trailing slash is enforced so that directory-only ignore patterns (e.g., build/) match correctly. The first specification whose match_file() returns True short-circuits the evaluation and returns True.

Parameters: * gitignore_specs (dict[str, pathspec.PathSpec]): Dictionary mapping absolute directory paths to their compiled pathspec.PathSpec objects. * abs_path (str): The absolute filesystem path of the file or directory being evaluated. * is_dir (bool, optional): Flag indicating if the target path is a directory (True) or a file (False). Defaults to False.

Returns: * bool: True if abs_path matches any applicable in-scope .gitignore rule; otherwise False.

Example: 

# Internal call site within crawl_local_files() directory evaluation
if _matches_any_gitignore(gitignore_specs, abs_d, is_dir=True):
    reason = reason_gitignore

docs.text:
The primary return payload returned by crawl_local_files() matches the schema produced by crawl_github_files.py, allowing workflow nodes in nodes.py to ingest repositories agnostic of their source.

Field Type Description files dict[str, str] Mapping where keys are relative filepaths (or absolute paths if use_relative_paths=False) and values are UTF-8 decoded file text contents.

    "files": {
        "utils/crawl_local_files.py": "import fnmatch\nimport os\n...",
        "utils/call_llm.py": "import json\nimport logging\n...",

docs.title: Gitignore Specs Registry (gitignore_specs)
docs.text:
Internal mapping used during single-pass traversal to manage multi-level, nested .gitignore files across the filesystem hierarchy.

Key Value Type Description abs_dir_path (str) pathspec.PathSpec The absolute directory path containing the .gitignore file, serving as the relative root for pattern matching.

docs.title: Ingestion Telemetry State Counters
docs.text:
Internal tracking state maintained within crawl_local_files() and pushed to utils.output.emit() throughout the crawl lifecycle:

Counter / Collection Type Description entry_num int Sequential index of all encountered filesystem items (files and directories). count_processed int Total count of files successfully read and added to files_dict. count_excluded int Total count of files and directories rejected via .gitignore, exclude patterns, or include mismatches. count_size_limit int Total count of files rejected because their size exceeded max_file_size. count_non_text int Total count of files rejected due to binary encoding, decoding failures, or read exceptions. skipped_size_limit list[str] List of relative filepaths skipped due to the byte size ceiling. skipped_non_text list[str] List of relative filepaths skipped due to non-text content or read errors.

docs.title: Directory Existence Validation
docs.text:
crawl_local_files() performs explicit pre-validation on the target path: 

if not os.path.isdir(directory):
    raise ValueError(f"Directory does not exist: {directory}")
If the path does not exist, or points to a regular file rather than a directory, execution halts immediately with a ValueError.

docs.title: Robust Gitignore Loading
docs.text:
To prevent malformed .gitignore files from crashing the ingestion pipeline, _load_gitignore() catches all exceptions during file I/O and pattern compilation: 

try:
    with open(gitignore_path, encoding="utf-8-sig") as f:
        return pathspec.PathSpec.from_lines("gitwildmatch", f.readlines())
except Exception:
    return None
Any read failure or syntax error results in None, allowing traversal to proceed with remaining active patterns.

docs.title: Binary and Decoding Fault Isolation
docs.text:
When reading file contents, crawl_local_files() wraps the open() context in a dual-layer exception handler: 

try:
    with open(filepath, encoding="utf-8-sig") as f:
        content = f.read()
    files_dict[relpath] = content
    count_processed += 1
    emit("CRAWL_FILE_PROCESSED", num=entry_num, path=relpath)
except (UnicodeDecodeError, ValueError):
    count_non_text += 1
    skipped_non_text.append(relpath)
    emit("CRAWL_FILE_NOT_TEXT", num=entry_num, path=relpath)
except Exception as e:
    count_non_text += 1
    skipped_non_text.append(relpath)
    emit("CRAWL_FILE_ERROR", num=entry_num, path=relpath, error=e)
- UnicodeDecodeError and ValueError: Raised when attempting to read compiled binaries, compressed archives, images, or files with incompatible character encodings. These are treated as non-text assets, recorded in skipped_non_text, and emitted as CRAWL_FILE_NOT_TEXT. - Exception: Traps permission errors, broken symlinks, or transient OS filesystem locks, reporting the specific error object via CRAWL_FILE_ERROR without terminating the crawl.

docs.title: exclude_patterns.py
docs.text:
Source: utils/exclude_patterns.py

Following the local filesystem crawler architecture documented in crawl_local_files.py, this module provides the central repository of default file and directory ignore rules.

docs.title: Technical Overview
docs.text:
utils/exclude_patterns.py defines the canonical baseline of path exclusion rules for the Codebase-Knowledge-Builder system. During repository ingestion—whether executed locally via crawl_local_files.py or remotely via crawl_github_files.py—the extraction engine traverses directory trees containing thousands of files. Without aggressive pre-filtering, large language model (LLM) context windows are rapidly exhausted by binary media, compiled bytecode, dependency trees, lockfiles, minified distribution bundles, and AI tool metadata. This module acts as the declarative filter configuration that prunes irrelevant artifacts before they reach downstream token counting and LLM inference pipelines.

The module exports a single primary data structure: DEFAULT_EXCLUDE_PATTERNS, a Python set containing Unix shell-style glob patterns compatible with standard fnmatch matching algorithms. The patterns are systematically partitioned across seven technical domains: static assets, build distributions, dependency directories, language-specific runtime artifacts, version control systems, legacy IDE metadata, and modern AI coding assistant telemetry. Directory patterns explicitly terminate with the /* wildcard syntax, enabling crawler implementations to prune entire directory branches during traversal rather than processing child paths individually.

docs.title: DEFAULT_EXCLUDE_PATTERNS
docs.text:
Visibility: Public (Module Constant)

Signature: 

DEFAULT_EXCLUDE_PATTERNS: set[str]

Description: A constant hash set containing 131 default glob patterns used to identify non-source, binary, generated, dependency, or metadata files across diverse software ecosystems. Downstream crawlers consume this set to perform pattern matching against relative directory paths and individual filenames using fnmatch.fnmatch() or directory-level prefix pruning.

The set employs three syntactic conventions: 1. Directory subtrees (<dir>/*): Used for early pruning during filesystem walking (e.g., node_modules/*, __pycache__/*, .git/*). 2. File extensions (*.<ext>): Used for filtering binary media, compiled bytecode, libraries, and compressed archives (e.g., *.png, *.pyc, *.dll, *.zip). 3. Exact filenames (<filename>): Used for configuration files, lockfiles, and environment definitions that contain excessive or sensitive data (e.g., package-lock.json, .DS_Store, .env).
