The declarative grouping allows engine developers to extend or prune rules without altering crawling algorithms in crawl_local_files.py or crawl_github_files.py.

docs.title: Pattern Category Taxonomy
docs.text: DEFAULT_EXCLUDE_PATTERNS is structurally organized into seven domain-specific categories. The following tables document each pattern, its syntax matching type, target ecosystem, and technical rationale.

docs.title: 1. Media, Data, and Static Assets
docs.text:
Static binary assets, multimedia files, office documents, and compressed archives cannot be meaningfully summarized as plain text by LLMs and risk encoding corruption or token overflow.

Pattern Match Type Target Domain Technical Rationale assets/* Directory Prefix Web / App Assets Static resource directory containing bundled images, fonts, and stylesheets. data/* Directory Prefix Datasets / Fixtures Raw application data, SQLite databases, or bulky JSON/CSV records. images/* Directory Prefix Graphics Storage Raster and vector images used across UI interfaces. public/* Directory Prefix Frontend Bundles Static web assets served directly without build transformations. static/* Directory Prefix Backend Frameworks Static directory convention (Django, Flask, FastAPI) for CSS/JS/images. temp/* Directory Prefix Temporary Files Ephemeral scratch directory for runtime file generation. tmp/* Directory Prefix Temporary Files Unix-style temporary directory. media/* Directory Prefix User Media Uploaded user content and multimedia storage. *.jpg, *.jpeg File Extension Raster Image Binary JPEG image format. *.png File Extension Raster Image Binary PNG image format. *.gif File Extension Raster Image Binary GIF animation format. *.ico File Extension Raster Image Binary favicon icon format. *.svg File Extension Vector Graphic XML-based vector graphics that contain high token counts with low logic value. *.webp File Extension Raster Image Modern compressed image format. *.mp4, *.webm, *.mov File Extension Video Media Binary video container formats. *.mp3, *.wav File Extension Audio Media Binary audio container formats. *.pdf File Extension Document Portable Document Format binary structure. *.doc, *.docx File Extension Document Microsoft Word legacy binary and OpenXML compressed archive formats. *.xls, *.xlsx File Extension Spreadsheet Microsoft Excel tabular sheets containing non-code binary structures. *.ppt, *.pptx File Extension Presentation Microsoft PowerPoint presentation files. *.zip, *.tar, *.gz, *.rar, *.7z File Extension Archive Compressed multi-file container archives.

docs.title: 2. Build, Distribution, and Framework Caches
docs.text:
Generated compiler outputs, framework intermediate bundles, log files, and test caches do not represent original source logic.

Pattern Match Type Target Domain Technical Rationale dist/* Directory Prefix Build Distribution Compiled production bundles for JavaScript, Python wheels, etc. build/* Directory Prefix Build System Generic build target directory for C, C++, Python, and JS. out/* Directory Prefix Compiler Output Output directory for TypeScript, Go, and IntelliJ builds. output/* Directory Prefix Artifact Storage General artifact export directory. output-test*/* Directory Prefix Test Harness Test runner output and mock generation artifacts. target/* Directory Prefix Rust / Maven Rust Cargo and Java Maven build output root. bin/* Directory Prefix Executables Compiled binary executables and execution scripts. obj/* Directory Prefix C / C++ / .NET Intermediate compiled object files. .next/* Directory Prefix Next.js Next.js server and client bundle cache. .nuxt/* Directory Prefix Nuxt.js Nuxt framework cache and virtual entrypoints. .svelte-kit/* Directory Prefix SvelteKit SvelteKit routing manifest and build cache. .expo/* Directory Prefix React Native / Expo Expo mobile development tooling cache. docs/* Directory Prefix Documentation External documentation trees (often redundant to inline docs). test/*, tests/* Directory Prefix Test Suites Unit and integration test trees excluded during core architectural passes. examples/* Directory Prefix Examples Sample codebases and usage demonstrations. v1/* Directory Prefix API Versions Legacy API versions excluded to focus on active architecture. experimental/* Directory Prefix Prototypes Unreleased or non-production experimental spikes. deprecated/* Directory Prefix Legacy Code Code marked for removal. misc/*, legacy/* Directory Prefix Utility / Old Code Unstructured utility scripts and legacy assets. *.log File Extension Logging Runtime execution log traces. *.bak, *.tmp, *.swp File Extension Editor / Temp Backup files, temporary writes, and Vim swap files.

docs.title: 3. Environments, Dependencies & Lockfiles
docs.text:
Third-party dependencies and machine-generated lockfiles contain tens of thousands of lines that dilute repository-specific logic and exhaust LLM context.

Pattern Match Type Target Domain Technical Rationale venv/*, .venv/*, env/* Directory Prefix Python Virtualenv Isolated Python runtime environments and site-packages. .env, .env.* Exact / Glob Secrets & Config Local environment variable definitions containing credentials and API keys. node_modules/* Directory Prefix Node.js Ecosystem NPM, Yarn, and PNPM resolved dependency trees. bower_components/* Directory Prefix Bower Package Manager Legacy client-side package dependencies. jspm_packages/* Directory Prefix JSPM SystemJS/JSPM package repository. vendor/* Directory Prefix Go / PHP / Ruby Vendored dependencies for Go modules, Composer, or Bundler. packages/* Directory Prefix Monorepos / NuGet Local monorepo dependency cache or NuGet package directory. *.lock File Extension General Lockfiles Generic dependency resolution lockfiles. package-lock.json Exact Match NPM NPM resolved dependency tree and checksum manifest. yarn.lock Exact Match Yarn Yarn resolved package graph. pnpm-lock.yaml Exact Match PNPM PNPM content-addressable storage lockfile. Cargo.lock Exact Match Rust / Cargo Exact crate dependency versions for Rust projects. Gemfile.lock Exact Match Ruby / Bundler Ruby gem dependency resolution state. poetry.lock Exact Match Python Poetry Poetry pinned dependency hashes and versions. mix.lock Exact Match Elixir / Mix Hex package lockfile for Elixir applications. Pipfile.lock Exact Match Pipenv JSON-formatted dependency hash lockfile for Pipenv.

docs.title: 4. Language-Specific Exclusions
docs.text:
Language compilers, runtime virtual machines, and testing harnesses generate intermediate binaries, bytecode, and coverage metrics that cannot be read as plain text.

Pattern Match Type Ecosystem Technical Rationale __pycache__/* Directory Prefix Python CPython compiled bytecode directory. *.pyc, *.pyo, *.pyd File Extension Python Compiled bytecode, optimized bytecode, and C-extension DLLs. .pytest_cache/* Directory Prefix Python (pytest) Pytest execution cache and step failure state. .ruff_cache/* Directory Prefix Python (Ruff) Ruff linter file analysis cache. .tox/* Directory Prefix Python (Tox) Tox virtual environment test runner matrices. .coverage, htmlcov/* Exact / Directory Python (Coverage) SQLite coverage database and generated HTML coverage reports. .gradle/* Directory Prefix Java / Kotlin / Gradle Gradle daemon cache, dependency cache, and build steps. *.class File Extension JVM Compiled Java bytecode binaries. *.jar, *.war, *.ear File Extension JVM Java ARchive, Web Application, and Enterprise Application packages. *.nar File Extension JVM / Native Native ARchive format for JVM native bindings. *.o, *.obj File Extension C / C++ / Native Compiled object code prior to linking. *.dll, *.dylib, *.so File Extension Native Libraries Dynamically linked shared libraries (Windows, macOS, Linux). *.exe File Extension Executable Windows portable executable binaries. *.lib, *.a File Extension Static Libraries Statically linked archive libraries (Windows, Unix). ios/Pods/* Directory Prefix iOS (CocoaPods) Downloaded CocoaPods library source dependencies. android/.gradle/* Directory Prefix Android Android Studio Gradle wrapper and daemon state. android/app/build/* Directory Prefix Android Android application intermediate APK and AAR build assets.

docs.title: 5. OS & Version Control
docs.text:
Internal version control databases and operating system file managers create metadata files containing binary indices or display configurations.

Pattern Match Type Target Domain Technical Rationale .git/* Directory Prefix Git Internal Git repository database (objects, refs, hooks, index). .github/* Directory Prefix GitHub CI/CD actions, issue templates, and repository workflows. .svn/* Directory Prefix Subversion Legacy SVN repository administrative directory. .hg/* Directory Prefix Mercurial Mercurial version control store. .DS_Store Exact Match macOS Finder Desktop Services Store containing folder view settings. Thumbs.db Exact Match Windows Explorer Thumbnail image cache for Windows folders. desktop.ini Exact Match Windows Explorer Custom folder layout and icon configuration file.

docs.title: 6. Classic IDEs
docs.text:
Integrated Development Environment project configurations, compiler workspace indices, and user-specific editor preferences.

Pattern Match Type IDE / Tool Technical Rationale .vscode/* Directory Prefix Visual Studio Code Workspace launch settings, extension recommendations, and tasks. .idea/* Directory Prefix JetBrains IDEs IntelliJ/PyCharm workspace state, indexing cache, and project models. *.iml File Extension JetBrains IDEs IntelliJ module configuration XML file. .eclipse/* Directory Prefix Eclipse IDE Eclipse project workspace metadata. .settings/* Directory Prefix Eclipse IDE Eclipse project-level plugin configuration. .classpath, .project Exact Match Eclipse IDE Eclipse Java build path and core project descriptors. .vs/* Directory Prefix Visual Studio Visual Studio solution browsing databases and debug sessions.

docs.title: 7. AI Agents & Modern AI IDEs
docs.text:
Modern AI development environments and autonomous coding agents generate prompt scratchpads, rule configurations, indexing databases, and session logs that distract repository comprehension models.

Pattern Match Type AI System Technical Rationale .cursor/* Directory Prefix Cursor IDE Cursor indexing database, project indexing state, and logs. .cursorrules Exact Match Cursor IDE Custom system instructions and project-level AI constraints. .windsurf/* Directory Prefix Windsurf IDE Codeium Windsurf project cache and execution traces. .windsurfrules Exact Match Windsurf IDE Windsurf agent system instructions. .cline/* Directory Prefix Cline Assistant Cline agent task memory, checkpoint history, and MCP settings. .clinerules Exact Match Cline Assistant Cline repository instruction set. .roo/* Directory Prefix Roo Code Roo Code agent task states and context histories. .roorules Exact Match Roo Code Roo Code custom rule configuration. .agent/*, .agents/* Directory Prefix Generic Agents Autonomous coding agent working directories and tool outputs. .continue/* Directory Prefix Continue.dev Continue indexing store, prompt templates, and telemetry. .aide/* Directory Prefix Aide IDE Aide workspace indexing and execution artifacts. .gemini/* Directory Prefix Gemini CLI / IDE Gemini assistant local project configuration and caches. .antigravity/* Directory Prefix Antigravity AI Antigravity engine workspace metadata and task traces. .claude/* Directory Prefix Anthropic Claude Claude Code CLI project settings and conversation logs. .copilot/* Directory Prefix GitHub Copilot Copilot workspace indexing state and local configuration.

docs.title: output.py
docs.text:
Source: utils/output.py

Following the path filtering rules defined in exclude_patterns.py, utils/output.py implements the centralized messaging, internationalization (i18n), terminal formatting, and diagnostic logging subsystem for the Codebase-Knowledge-Builder engine.

docs.title: Technical Overview
docs.text:
utils/output.py provides a unified output interface that abstracts terminal styling, file logging, and localized message resolution across the entire repository analysis pipeline. By decoupling message invocation from raw string literals and direct terminal input/output (I/O), the subsystem ensures that all user-facing diagnostics, operational metrics, LLM interaction alerts, and generated documentation UI strings can be dynamically translated, formatted with context-specific arguments, and routed selectively to STDOUT, dedicated log files, or internal document builders.

The module operates around an on-disk CSV localization store (utils/strings.csv). Upon startup, strings are parsed into memory. If non-English output is requested and translations for the target language are missing or incomplete, the module automatically delegates translation to the LLM subsystem via call_llm.py, persists the translated entries back into strings.csv with a UTF-8 Byte Order Mark (BOM) for Excel compatibility, and dynamically refreshes its internal lookup table. Output calls are routed through ANSI color palettes for terminal rendering and Python's native logging framework for persistent file-based tracing.

docs.title: init()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def init(language="english", use_cache=True, thinking_level=None) -> None

Description: Initializes the output subsystem by setting active language configurations, loading localization entries from strings.csv, and initiating automated LLM-driven translation for any missing strings in the target language. This must be invoked from the entry point (such as main.py) after parsing CLI flags and before calling emit().

Parameters: * language (str): Target language name for CLI output and generated documentation (e.g., "english", "vietnamese"). Defaults to "english". * use_cache (bool): Flag passed down to LLM calls during automated translation to enable or bypass response caching. Defaults to True. * thinking_level (str | None): Reasoning effort budget configuration passed to translation LLM calls. Defaults to None.

Returns: * None

Raises: * Does not raise directly; internal file errors or LLM translation failures are caught defensively, with warnings emitted to terminal and fallbacks to English.

Example: 

def init(language="english", use_cache=True, thinking_level=None):
    """Initialize the output system: load strings.csv, set language, auto-translate missing.

    Must be called from main() after parsing CLI arguments but before any emit() calls.

    Args:
        language: Target language name (e.g., "Vietnamese").
        use_cache: Whether LLM caching is enabled (passed to translation calls).
        thinking_level: LLM thinking level (passed to translation calls).
    """
    global _language, _lang_col, _csv_path, _use_cache, _thinking_level
    _language = language.capitalize()
    _lang_col = language.lower()
    _csv_path = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), "strings.csv")
    _use_cache = use_cache
    _thinking_level = thinking_level
    _load_strings()
    _auto_translate()

The function configures global module state pointers, determines the absolute path to strings.csv relative to output.py, and triggers _load_strings(). Once the baseline strings dictionary is assembled, _auto_translate() checks whether any records in the specified language column are empty, translating them as a single batch if necessary.

docs.title: emit()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def emit(key, suffix="", **kwargs) -> None

Description: Emits a localized, formatted string to standard output, the log file, or both, based on the record configuration in strings.csv. Applies variable substitutions safely via _format_safe(), appends any optional suffix text (such as token metrics), and applies terminal color codes according to the message's defined LEVEL.

Parameters: * key (str): String identifier matching a STRING_KEY entry in strings.csv (e.g., "LLM_CALL_WRITE_CHAPTER"). * suffix (str): Optional text appended directly to the formatted message before emission (useful for raw token breakdowns or latency metrics). Defaults to "". * **kwargs: Key-value pairs matching {placeholder} tags defined in the target string template.

Returns: * None

Raises: * Does not raise exceptions. If key is missing from _strings, a fallback message [UNKNOWN STRING: {key}] is printed directly to STDOUT.

Example: 

def emit(key, suffix="", **kwargs):
    """Emit a translatable string to stdout and/or log file.

    Args:
        key: String key from strings.csv (e.g., "LLM_CALL_WRITE_CHAPTER").
        suffix: Optional extra text appended after the main message (e.g., token breakdown).
        **kwargs: Variables to substitute into the string template.
    """
    entry = _strings.get(key)
    if not entry:
        # Fallback for unknown keys — print raw so nothing is silently lost
        print(f"[UNKNOWN STRING: {key}]")
        return

    text = _format_safe(entry["text"], kwargs)
    if suffix:
        text = text + suffix

    level = entry["level"]
    dest = entry["dest"]
    color = COLORS.get(level, "")
    reset = RESET if color else ""

    if dest in ("BOTH", "STDOUT"):
        print(f"{color}{text}{reset}")
    if dest in ("BOTH", "LOG"):
        _logger.log(LOG_LEVELS.get(level, logging.INFO), text)

The function queries _strings for the metadata dictionary associated with key. If found, _format_safe() interpolates the keyword arguments into entry["text"]. The message destination (entry["dest"]) dictates whether the styled payload is printed via print() to terminal with ANSI escape codes, logged to _logger using the mapped Python log level, or dispatched to both channels simultaneously.

docs.title: emit_raw()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def emit_raw(level, text, dest="BOTH") -> None

Description: Emits unmanaged, dynamically formatted text directly to terminal output or logging channels with explicit level-based ANSI color styling. Used for structural CLI output not tracked in strings.csv, such as file lists, dynamic progress tables, batch splits, and raw error messages.

Parameters: * level (str): The severity/style level matching a key in COLORS (e.g., "PROGRESS", "SUCCESS", "WARNING", "ERROR", "INFO", "DEBUG"). * text (str): The raw text message to be emitted. * dest (str): Target destination channel. Allowed values are "BOTH", "STDOUT", or "LOG". Defaults to "BOTH".

Returns: * None

Raises: * Does not raise exceptions.

Example: 

def emit_raw(level, text, dest="BOTH"):
    """Emit a pre-formatted string with explicit level styling.

    Use for dynamic/structural output that doesn't come from strings.csv
    (e.g., numbered file lists, batch details, crawl summary tables).
    """
    color = COLORS.get(level, "")
    reset = RESET if color else ""

    if dest in ("BOTH", "STDOUT"):
        print(f"{color}{text}{reset}")
    if dest in ("BOTH", "LOG"):
        _logger.log(LOG_LEVELS.get(level, logging.INFO), text)

emit_raw resolves ANSI styling directly from COLORS using the provided level identifier. If dest includes "STDOUT", it prints the colored message followed by an ANSI reset code. If dest includes "LOG", it resolves the corresponding logging level via LOG_LEVELS (defaulting to logging.INFO) and writes the uncolored string payload to _logger.

docs.title: get()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def get(key, **kwargs) -> str

Description: Resolves and returns a localized string without writing to terminal output or active log handlers. Used primarily by documentation generator nodes to retrieve localized section headers, table titles, and UI text elements embedded into generated markdown documents.

Parameters: * key (str): String key identifier present in strings.csv. * **kwargs: Key-value pairs for template placeholder variable substitution.

Returns: * str: The localized text string with all {placeholder} variables substituted, or the raw key if no matching record exists in _strings.

Raises: * Does not raise exceptions.

Example: 

def get(key, **kwargs):
    """Get a translated string without printing or logging.

    Use for UI strings embedded in generated markdown (index.md headings, etc.).
    Returns the raw translated text with variable substitution applied.
    """
    entry = _strings.get(key)
    if not entry:
        return key  # Fallback: return the key itself
    return _format_safe(entry["text"], kwargs)

The function accesses _strings to retrieve the active translation entry. If the key is not present, it gracefully returns key as a fallback. When an entry is found, it evaluates entry["text"] using _format_safe with the supplied kwargs dictionary, ensuring that UI labels can incorporate dynamic runtime numbers or paths without terminal formatting artifacts.

docs.title: configure_logging()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def configure_logging(project_name="project", mode="tutorial") -> str

Description: Configures file-based logging for the active execution run. Generates a timestamped log file inside the directory specified by the LOG_DIR environment variable (defaulting to logs/), clears any pre-existing handlers on _logger (such as logging.NullHandler), registers a UTF-8 FileHandler, and records execution metadata headers.

Parameters: * project_name (str): Name of the analyzed repository or target project, sanitized for filesystem safety. Defaults to "project". * mode (str): Active execution mode (e.g., "tutorial", "reference"). Defaults to "tutorial".

Returns: * str: The absolute or normalized path to the created log file on disk.

Raises: * OSError: If the log directory cannot be created due to filesystem permissions.

Example: 

def configure_logging(project_name="project", mode="tutorial"):
    """Configure file-based logging for this run.

    Creates a new log file per invocation:
        logs/{project_name}_{mode}_{YYYYMMDD_HHmmss}.log

    Must be called from main() after parsing CLI arguments.
    """
    from datetime import datetime

    log_directory = os.getenv("LOG_DIR", "logs")
    os.makedirs(log_directory, exist_ok=True)

    safe_project = "".join(c if c.isalnum() or c in "-_." else "_" for c in project_name)
    safe_mode = mode.replace("-", "_")
    timestamp = datetime.now().strftime("%Y%m%d_%H%M%S")
    log_file = os.path.join(log_directory, f"{safe_project}_{safe_mode}_{timestamp}.log")

    # Remove any existing handlers (e.g., NullHandler) and add the file handler
    _logger.handlers.clear()
    file_handler = logging.FileHandler(log_file, encoding="utf-8")
    file_handler.setFormatter(logging.Formatter("%(asctime)s - %(levelname)s - %(message)s"))
    _logger.addHandler(file_handler)

    # Log run metadata at the start of every log file
    _logger.info(f"{'=' * 80}")
    _logger.info(f"RUN STARTED | project={project_name} | mode={mode} | timestamp={timestamp}")
    _logger.info(f"Log file: {log_file}")
    _logger.info(f"{'=' * 80}")

    return log_file

configure_logging creates the log directory via os.makedirs(..., exist_ok=True). It sanitizes project_name by replacing non-alphanumeric characters (excluding -, _, and .) with underscores, formats the current timestamp into %Y%m%d_%H%M%S, and constructs the output file path. It flushes any pre-existing handlers on _logger, binds a logging.FileHandler using UTF-8 encoding, configures a standard timestamp-level-message formatter, and writes run-header metadata directly into the log file.

docs.title: _format_safe()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _format_safe(template: str, kwargs: dict) -> str

Description: Safely applies standard Python string formatting (str.format(**kwargs)) against a template string. Intercepts common formatting errors (such as missing placeholder variables, unescaped curly braces, or type mismatches) and returns the unformatted template intact rather than crashing the pipeline.

Parameters: * template (str): String containing optional {placeholder} replacement tokens. * kwargs (dict): Dictionary of keyword replacements.

Returns: * str: The successfully interpolated string, or the raw template if a formatting exception occurs.

Raises: * Does not raise exceptions; catches KeyError, IndexError, and ValueError.

Example: 

def _format_safe(template, kwargs):
    """Apply .format(**kwargs) with graceful fallback on missing keys."""
    try:
        return template.format(**kwargs)
    except (KeyError, IndexError, ValueError):
        return template

This helper wraps template.format(**kwargs) inside a defensive try-except block. In dynamic environments where LLMs or external configurations might pass partially populated variable sets, catching KeyError (missing placeholder value), IndexError (positional token mismatch), and ValueError (invalid format specification) guarantees that logging or CLI printing will not disrupt execution.

docs.title: _load_strings()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _load_strings() -> None

Description: Reads and parses utils/strings.csv into the internal _strings dictionary using csv.DictReader with utf-8-sig encoding. Extracts string identifiers, level tags, destination channels, and resolved text content (prioritizing the active language column with automatic fallback to the english column).

Parameters: * None (operates on module-level globals _csv_path, _lang_col, _language, and _strings).

Returns: * None

Raises: * Does not raise exceptions directly; missing files abort early, and CSV parsing handles BOM transparently.

Example: 

def _load_strings():
    """Load all strings from strings.csv."""
    global _strings
    _strings = {}

    if not _csv_path or not os.path.exists(_csv_path):
        return

    translated_count = 0
    total_count = 0

    with open(_csv_path, encoding="utf-8-sig") as f:
        reader = csv.DictReader(f)
        for row in reader:
            key = row.get("STRING_KEY", "").strip()
            if not key or key.startswith("#"):
                continue

            level = row.get("LEVEL", "INFO").strip()
            dest = row.get("DEST", "BOTH").strip()

            # Priority: language column → English fallback
            text = row.get(_lang_col, "").strip()
            if text:
                translated_count += 1
            else:
                text = row.get("english", "").strip()

            total_count += 1
            _strings[key] = {"text": text, "level": level, "dest": dest}

    if _lang_col != "english" and translated_count == total_count:
        emit_raw("SUCCESS", f"[i18n] {_language} — loaded {translated_count} strings from CSV")

The function clears _strings and iterates across all records in strings.csv. It skips empty rows and comment lines starting with #. For each valid key, it inspects the target language column (_lang_col). If a non-empty string exists, it increments translated_count; otherwise, it falls back to the value in the english column. If all keys for a non-English language are fully translated, a success message is emitted to terminal and log channels.

docs.title: _auto_translate()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _auto_translate() -> None

Description: Identifies missing translations for the active target language in strings.csv, constructs a batch translation prompt using prompts/common/translate_strings.md, calls the inference gateway via call_llm(), parses the returned JSON dictionary, writes new translations to strings.csv, and reloads the memory state.

docs.title: Phase 1: Target Language and CSV Pre-check
docs.text:
def _auto_translate():
    """Auto-translate missing strings via LLM and write back into strings.csv."""
    if _lang_col == "english":
        return

    if not _csv_path or not os.path.exists(_csv_path):
        return
Phase 1 checks whether translation is necessary. If the target language is English or if strings.csv is inaccessible, execution terminates immediately without reading records or triggering LLM calls.

docs.title: Phase 2: Missing Translation Discovery
docs.text:
# Collect strings that have no translation in the target language column
    missing = {}
    is_new_column = False
    with open(_csv_path, encoding="utf-8-sig") as f:
        reader = csv.DictReader(f)
        fieldnames = list(reader.fieldnames)
        is_new_column = _lang_col not in fieldnames
        for row in reader:
            key = row.get("STRING_KEY", "").strip()
            if not key or key.startswith("#"):
                continue
            # Check if the language column exists and has a value
            lang_text = row.get(_lang_col, "").strip() if _lang_col in fieldnames else ""
            if lang_text:
                continue  # Already translated

            english_text = row.get("english", "").strip()
            if english_text:
                missing[key] = english_text

    if not missing:
        return

    # Report what we found
    if is_new_column:
        emit_raw("PROGRESS", f"[i18n] New language '{_language}' — adding column to strings.csv")
    emit_raw("PROGRESS", f"[i18n] {len(missing)} strings need translation to {_language}")
Phase 2 parses strings.csv to detect whether the target language column exists in reader.fieldnames. It traverses every non-comment row to collect keys where the target column is missing or empty, mapping key -> english_text into the missing dictionary. If all strings are translated, the function returns. Otherwise, it emits progress messages indicating how many translations are required.

docs.title: Phase 3: Prompt Construction & LLM Request Execution
docs.text:
# Batch translate via LLM
    try:
        from utils.call_llm import call_llm

        entries_json = json.dumps(missing, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2)

        # Load prompt template from prompts/common/translate_strings.md
        prompt_path = os.path.join(
            os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))),
            "prompts",
            "common",
            "translate_strings.md",
        )
        with open(prompt_path, encoding="utf-8") as pf:
            prompt_template = pf.read()
        prompt = prompt_template.format(language=_language, entries=entries_json)

        emit_raw("PROGRESS", f"[i18n] Calling LLM to translate {len(missing)} strings...")
        response = call_llm(prompt, use_cache=_use_cache, thinking_level=_thinking_level)
Phase 3 dynamically imports call_llm from call_llm.py (preventing circular import loops at module initialization). It formats the missing dictionary into a JSON string, loads the translation prompt template from prompts/common/translate_strings.md, and sends the prompt payload to the configured LLM provider with the caching and thinking level settings established during init().

docs.title: Phase 4: Response Parsing, CSV Persistence, and Memory Reload
docs.text:
# Extract JSON from response
        json_match = re.search(r"\{[^{}]*(?:\{[^{}]*\}[^{}]*)*\}", response, re.DOTALL)
        if json_match:
            translations = json.loads(json_match.group())
            translated_count = len(translations)

            # Write translations back into strings.csv
            _write_translations_to_csv(translations)
            emit_raw("SUCCESS", f"[i18n] Translated {translated_count}/{len(missing)} strings — saved to strings.csv")

            # Reload strings from the updated CSV so all translations are active
            _load_strings()
        else:
            emit_raw("WARNING", "[i18n] LLM response did not contain valid JSON — falling back to English")

    except Exception as e:
        emit_raw("WARNING", f"[i18n] Translation failed: {e} — falling back to English")
Phase 4 extracts the JSON translation dictionary from the model response using a regular expression. It parses the JSON payload, passes the resulting dictionary to _write_translations_to_csv(), and invokes _load_strings() to refresh in-memory strings with the new translations. If JSON extraction or inference fails, defensive exception handling logs a warning and leaves English fallbacks active.

docs.title: _write_translations_to_csv()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _write_translations_to_csv(translations: dict[str, str]) -> None

Description: Updates strings.csv on disk with newly translated strings. If the target language column does not already exist in the CSV header, it appends the new column and writes all rows with UTF-8 BOM encoding (utf-8-sig) and blank line controls.

Parameters: * translations (dict[str, str]): Dictionary mapping STRING_KEY names to their newly translated text strings.

Returns: * None

Raises: * OSError: If the file cannot be written due to disk or permission constraints.

Example: 

def _write_translations_to_csv(translations):
    """Write LLM translations back into strings.csv, persisting them for future runs.

    If the target language column doesn't exist, it is added to the CSV.
    """
    rows = []
    fieldnames = None

    with open(_csv_path, encoding="utf-8-sig") as f:
        reader = csv.DictReader(f)
        fieldnames = list(reader.fieldnames)
        # Add language column if it doesn't exist
        if _lang_col not in fieldnames:
            fieldnames.append(_lang_col)
        for row in reader:
            key = row.get("STRING_KEY", "").strip()
            if key in translations:
                row[_lang_col] = translations[key]
            rows.append(row)

    # Write with BOM so Excel opens as UTF-8 without extra import steps
    with open(_csv_path, "w", encoding="utf-8-sig", newline="") as f:
        writer = csv.DictWriter(f, fieldnames=fieldnames)
        writer.writeheader()
        writer.writerows(rows)

The function reads all existing rows and column headers from strings.csv. If _lang_col is not present in fieldnames, it appends the new column name to the header list. It iterates through all rows, updating the target language field for any key matching translations. Finally, it opens _csv_path with utf-8-sig encoding and newline="" to prevent blank lines on Windows platforms, re-writing the updated dataset via csv.DictWriter.

docs.title: Error Handling
docs.text:
The module employs defensive error handling to prevent logging or formatting errors from halting the knowledge generation pipeline:

  • Unknown String Keys: When emit() receives a key not present in _strings, it avoids raising KeyError. Instead, it outputs [UNKNOWN STRING: {key}] to standard output to maintain pipeline progress while alerting developers to the missing entry.
  • Template Formatting Fallbacks: In _format_safe(), string interpolation errors (KeyError, IndexError, ValueError) are caught and suppressed, returning the raw template string unmodified.
  • Auto-Translation Failures: In _auto_translate(), LLM communication errors, network failures, and JSON decoding issues are wrapped in a general except Exception as e: block. The error is emitted as a WARNING via emit_raw(), and the module transparently falls back to the canonical English strings in memory without crashing the process.
  • Missing CSV File Handling: Both _load_strings() and _auto_translate() verify os.path.exists(_csv_path) before attempting file I/O, allowing the module to fail gracefully if the strings table is deleted or misplaced.

docs.title: utils.prompts
docs.text:
Source File Path: utils/prompts.py

The utils.prompts module contains reusable, programmatic prompt builders and documentation scaffolding utilities for internal system routines in Codebase-Knowledge-Builder. While mode-specific architectural prompts are loaded from structured external templates (prompts/{mode}/), utils.prompts manages programmatic prompt constructions for deterministic file filtering and cross-chapter contextual summarization, as well as configuration generators for local MkDocs exports (YAML config generation, Mermaid CSS overrides, and recursive navigation hierarchy construction).

docs.title: Architectural Role and Workflow
docs.text:
The functions in utils.prompts are utilized across distinct stages of the documentation pipeline:

  1. Deterministic File Filtering: Pre-generation phase where non-code assets, configurations, and build artifacts are stripped out via zero-shot/few-shot index extraction prompts.
  2. Contextual Chapter Summaries: Intra-generation feedback loop where completed chapters are summarized into structured four-dimensional technical briefs, providing continuous architectural context to subsequent chapter nodes.
  3. MkDocs Site & Navigation Assembly: Post-generation serialization phase where the table of contents hierarchy is parsed, matched to generated markdown files, styled with high-contrast Mermaid CSS rules, and written into a standalone mkdocs.yml.

docs.title: build_code_file_filter_prompt()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def build_code_file_filter_prompt(project_name: str, file_listing: str) -> str:

Description: Constructs an LLM prompt string designed for DeterministicFileMapper in API reference extraction pipelines. The prompt instructs the language model to review an indexed list of repository file paths and return a clean YAML array of integer indices corresponding exclusively to source code files (modules containing functions, classes, and business logic). It explicitly specifies exclusion rules for UI layout files, configuration files, build scripts, static assets, and documentation.

Parameters: * project_name (str): The name of the target repository or codebase being processed. * file_listing (str): Formatted string containing the indexed repository file paths (e.g., 0: src/main.py\n1: config.json).

Returns: * str: The complete, formatted prompt ready to be dispatched to the LLM via utils.call_llm.

Raises: * None.

Example: 

def build_code_file_filter_prompt(project_name: str, file_listing: str) -> str:
    """Build the prompt for DeterministicFileMapper to filter non-code files.

    Used in api-reference mode to identify which files are actual code modules
    (APIs, functions, classes, business logic) vs. UI layouts, configs, assets.
    """
    return (
        f"For the project `{project_name}`, here is the list of all files in the codebase:\n\n"
        f"{file_listing}\n\n"
        f"Your task is to identify WHICH of these files are ACTUAL CODE files that contain "
        f"APIs, functions, classes, or core business logic.\n"
        f"EXCLUDE: UI layouts (like .xaml, .storyboard, .html), configuration files "
        f"(like .xml, .json, .manifest, .ini), static assets, build scripts "
        f"(like .csproj, .sln), and documentation.\n\n"
        f"Return ONLY a YAML list of the file indices that should be documented as code modules.\n\n"
        f"```yaml\n- 0\n- 1\n- 3\n```"
    )

The prompt structure enforces a strict output constraint (Return ONLY a YAML list of the file indices) with a few-shot markdown fence example. By operating on integer indices rather than raw file paths, the prompt minimizes token generation overhead during the LLM filtering pass and guarantees reliable programmatic parsing.

docs.title: build_chapter_summary_prompt()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def build_chapter_summary_prompt(chapter_num: int, abstraction_name: str, chapter_content: str, language: str = "english") -> str:

Description: Generates a structured prompt to summarize a previously generated chapter across four standardized technical dimensions. The resulting brief acts as historical memory and is prepended to subsequent chapter generation prompts within nodes to preserve cross-module coherence, maintain terminology consistency, and prevent duplicate explanations. The summary evaluates component scope, key classes/functions, implementation patterns/architectural decisions, and inter-component dependencies.

Parameters: * chapter_num (int): The ordinal sequence number of the completed chapter. * abstraction_name (str): The chapter's title or architectural component identifier. * chapter_content (str): The full Markdown text generated for the specified chapter. * language (str, optional): The target output natural language. Defaults to "english".

Returns: * str: A prompt string instructing the model to generate 3–5 technical sentences for each of the four structural dimensions.

Raises: * None.

Example: 

def build_chapter_summary_prompt(chapter_num: int, abstraction_name: str, chapter_content: str, language: str = "english") -> str:
    lang_instruction = f"Write the entire summary in {language.capitalize()}. " if language.lower() != "english" else ""
    return (
        f"{lang_instruction}"
        f"Summarize the following documentation chapter as a structured technical brief. "
        f"For EACH of the 4 points below, write 3-5 concise technical sentences:\n\n"
        f"(1) **Component Scope & Responsibility**: What is the main technical domain this "
        f"chapter covers? What problems does it solve and what role does it play in the system?\n\n"
        f"(2) **Key Technical Elements**: What are the specific classes, services, functions, "
        f"data models, or protocols discussed? Name them and describe their concrete roles.\n\n"
        f"(3) **Implementation Patterns & Architecture**: What design patterns, communication "
        f"protocols, data flow strategies, error handling mechanisms, or security measures "
        f"are covered? How are they implemented?\n\n"
        f"(4) **System Integration & Dependencies**: How does this component interface with "
        f"other parts of the system? What does it consume from or provide to other components? "
        f"What are the key integration points?\n\n"
        f"---\n"
        f"Chapter {chapter_num}: {abstraction_name}\n"
        f"{chapter_content}"
    )

The function incorporates conditional prefixing: if language is anything other than "english", a directive is prepended forcing the model to emit the brief in the requested target language. The prompt strictly limits the response length per section (3–5 sentences) to ensure that the accumulated summary context fits comfortably within downstream token budgets managed by utils.token_utils.

docs.title: build_mkdocs_config()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def build_mkdocs_config(site_name: str, nav_yaml: str) -> str:

Description: Assembles a complete, production-ready mkdocs.yml configuration string for rendering the documentation via Material for MkDocs. Configures the Material theme, dark/light mode toggles, search plugins, panzoom for interactive Mermaid diagram navigation, PyMdown Extensions syntax highlighting, custom super-fences for Mermaid diagram formatting, and extra CSS references.

Parameters: * site_name (str): The human-readable title displayed in the documentation header and browser tab. * nav_yaml (str): A YAML-formatted navigation block containing the mapped hierarchy of generated files.

Returns: * str: A valid, multi-line YAML document string ready to be saved to mkdocs.yml.

Raises: * None.

Example: 

def build_mkdocs_config(site_name: str, nav_yaml: str) -> str:
    # Extract nav items from nav_snippet (strip the "nav:" header line)
    nav_lines = nav_yaml.split("\n")
    nav_body = "\n".join(nav_lines[1:]) if nav_lines else ""

    return (
        f"site_name: '{site_name}'\n"
        f"theme:\n"
        f"  name: material\n"
        f"  features:\n"
        f"    - content.code.copy\n"
        f"    - navigation.indexes\n"
        f"  palette:\n"
        f"    - scheme: default\n"
        f"      toggle:\n"
        f"        icon: material/brightness-7\n"
        f"        name: Switch to dark mode\n"
        f"    - scheme: slate\n"
        f"      toggle:\n"
        f"        icon: material/brightness-4\n"
        f"        name: Switch to light mode\n"
        f"plugins:\n"
        f"  - search\n"
        f"  - panzoom:\n"
        f"      include_selectors:\n"
        f"        - '.mermaid'\n"
        f"markdown_extensions:\n"
        f"  - pymdownx.highlight:\n"
        f"      anchor_linenums: true\n"
        f"      use_pygments: true\n"
        f"  - pymdownx.superfences:\n"
        f"      custom_fences:\n"
        f"        - name: mermaid\n"
        f"          class: mermaid\n"
        f"          format: !!python/name:pymdownx.superfences.fence_code_format\n"
        f"  - pymdownx.inlinehilite\n"
        f"extra_css:\n"
        f"  - stylesheets/mermaid-vibrant.css\n"
        f"nav:\n"
        f"  - Home: index.md\n"
        f"{nav_body}\n"
    )

The function normalizes incoming nav_yaml blocks by removing any leading nav: declaration to prevent duplicate top-level keys in the final YAML configuration. It enforces code block copying (content.code.copy), index navigation (navigation.indexes), and registers !!python/name:pymdownx.superfences.fence_code_format so that Mermaid diagram blocks are rendered as interactive vector graphics rather than raw preformatted code blocks.

docs.title: build_mermaid_css()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def build_mermaid_css() -> str:

Description: Returns raw CSS stylesheet content that overrides default Material for MkDocs Mermaid theme color styles. Material for MkDocs suppresses default Mermaid %%{init}%% palette configurations; this stylesheet restores distinct styling featuring yellow cluster/subgraph fills, lavender node rectangles/polygons, purple node borders, and explicit dark text colors.

Parameters: * None.

Returns: * str: Raw CSS string containing rules for .mermaid .cluster, .mermaid .node, .mermaid .nodeLabel, .mermaid .edgeLabel, and .mermaid .edge-pattern-solid.

Raises: * None.

Example: 

def build_mermaid_css() -> str:
    """Build CSS overrides for vibrant Mermaid diagrams in MkDocs Material.

    Material for MkDocs forcibly overrides Mermaid's %%{init}%% directives,
    so we use CSS to restore vibrant colors matching Mermaid's default theme:
    - Yellow subgraph backgrounds
    - Lavender node fills
    - Purple node strokes
    """
    return """\
/* Vibrant Mermaid diagram theme — overrides Material's muted colors */
/* Matches Mermaid's built-in 'default' theme (yellow subgraphs, lavender nodes) */

/* Subgraph/cluster backgrounds — warm yellow */
.mermaid .cluster rect {
  fill: #ffffde !important;
  stroke: #aaaa33 !important;
  stroke-width: 1px !important;
}

/* Cluster/subgraph title text */
.mermaid .cluster text {
  fill: #333 !important;
}

/* Node fills — light lavender */
.mermaid .node rect,
.mermaid .node polygon,
.mermaid .node circle {
  fill: #ECECFF !important;
  stroke: #9370DB !important;
  stroke-width: 1px !important;
}

/* Node text */
.mermaid .nodeLabel {
  color: #333 !important;
}

/* Edge label backgrounds */
.mermaid .edgeLabel {
  background-color: #e8e8e8 !important;
  color: #333 !important;
}

/* Edge lines */
.mermaid .edge-pattern-solid {
  stroke: #333 !important;
}
"""

The returned CSS uses !important declarations to supersede Material's low-contrast CSS variables. This ensures that architectural diagrams generated across chapters remain legible in both light and dark display modes without requiring manual chart-by-chart style declarations.

docs.title: build_grouped_nav()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def build_grouped_nav(sections: list, chapter_files: list, indent: int = 4) -> list[str]:

Description: Recursively constructs lines of YAML text representing the MkDocs navigation hierarchy from an arbitrary tree of LLM-generated section structures. For each section, it checks for nested sub-sections under the children key and recurses with increased indentation. For leaf nodes (listed under modules), it searches chapter_files for a matching module_name and formats the entry to point to api/{match['filename']}.

Parameters: * sections (list): A list of dictionary objects describing sections. Each dictionary may contain "name" (str), "children" (list), and "modules" (list[str]). * chapter_files (list): A list of dictionaries representing generated chapter files, where each dictionary contains at least "module_name" and "filename". * indent (int, optional): Number of leading whitespace characters for the current indentation level. Defaults to 4.

Returns: * list[str]: A list of properly indented YAML string lines representing the navigation tree.

Raises: * None.

Example: 

def build_grouped_nav(sections: list, chapter_files: list, indent: int = 4) -> list[str]:
    """Recursively build MkDocs nav YAML lines from LLM section grouping.

    Handles arbitrary nesting depth via the ``children`` key.
    Each leaf module is matched against *chapter_files* by ``module_name``.
    """
    lines = []
    pad = " " * indent
    for section in sections:
        lines.append(f"{pad}- {section['name']}:")
        if "children" in section:
            lines.extend(build_grouped_nav(section["children"], chapter_files, indent + 2))
        for mod_name in section.get("modules", []):
            match = next((cf for cf in chapter_files if cf["module_name"] == mod_name), None)
            if match:
                display = mod_name.split(".")[-1] if "." in mod_name else mod_name
                lines.append(f"{pad}  - '{display}': 'api/{match['filename']}'")
    return lines

If a module name contains dots (e.g., utils.prompts), build_grouped_nav splits the name by . and uses only the terminal token (prompts) as the visible navigation label, while preserving the full matching path to the physical markdown target file. If a module specified in sections is not present in chapter_files, it is skipped without raising an error.

docs.title: collect_all_modules()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def collect_all_modules(sections: list) -> set:

Description: Performs a recursive tree traversal over a hierarchical section definition to extract and aggregate all referenced module names into a flat Python set. This utility is used to audit generated sections against discovered source files, identifying unmapped modules or verifying that no duplicate entries exist in the navigation tree.

Parameters: * sections (list): A list of dictionary trees, where each node contains an optional "modules" list and an optional "children" list of sub-sections.

Returns: * set: An unordered set containing every distinct module name string found across all depths of the section tree.

Raises: * None.

Example: 

def collect_all_modules(sections: list) -> set:
    """Recursively collect all module names referenced in a sections tree."""
    result = set()
    for section in sections:
        result.update(section.get("modules", []))
        if "children" in section:
            result.update(collect_all_modules(section["children"]))
    return result

This function traverses nested dictionaries without depth limits, avoiding module name duplication via Python set union operations (set.update). It handles sparse nodes gracefully by using .get("modules", []).

docs.title: prompts.py
docs.text:
Source: utils/prompts.py

While utils/output.py manages localized console output, user-facing diagnostics, and real-time terminal telemetry, utils/prompts.py acts as the programmatic template and artifact generation engine for the Codebase-Knowledge-Builder system. It centralizes inline prompt construction routines and static asset synthesis required for documentation site compilation, eliminating ad-hoc string formatting across workflow execution nodes.

docs.title: Technical Overview
docs.text:
utils/prompts.py serves two distinct functional roles within the system architecture: inline Large Language Model (LLM) prompt engineering and static documentation site compilation. Unlike mode-specific document prompts that are loaded from external Markdown templates (such as prompts/{mode}/), the prompts generated in this module are programmatic, structured payloads designed for internal deterministic operations. These include filtering non-code files during repository analysis and compressing generated chapters into dense technical briefs for cross-chapter context chaining.

In its second role, the module provides configuration and script builders for generating static documentation sites using MkDocs. It handles the dynamic assembly of mkdocs.yml configuration files, client-side JavaScript initializers for Mermaid diagram rendering, and the recursive compilation of nested navigation trees based on LLM section groupings and repository directory structures.

docs.title: build_code_file_filter_prompt()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def build_code_file_filter_prompt(project_name: str, file_listing: str) -> str:

Description: Generates an inline prompt instructing the LLM to act as a deterministic file mapper. It takes a complete list of repository files and prompts the model to return a strict YAML list containing only the integer indices of files that represent executable or API-relevant source code (e.g., classes, functions, business logic), filtering out UI layouts, configuration files, static assets, build manifests, and documentation.

Parameters: * project_name (str): The name of the target repository or project being analyzed. * file_listing (str): A formatted string representing repository file indices and relative paths.

Returns: * str: A formatted prompt ready for submission to call_llm().

Raises: * None.

Example: 

def build_code_file_filter_prompt(project_name: str, file_listing: str) -> str:
    """Build the prompt for DeterministicFileMapper to filter non-code files.

    Used in api-reference mode to identify which files are actual code modules
    (APIs, functions, classes, business logic) vs. UI layouts, configs, assets.
    """
    return (
        f"For the project `{project_name}`, here is the list of all files in the codebase:\n\n"
        f"{file_listing}\n\n"
        f"Your task is to identify WHICH of these files are ACTUAL CODE files that contain "
        f"APIs, functions, classes, or core business logic.\n"
        f"EXCLUDE: UI layouts (like .xaml, .storyboard, .html), configuration files "
        f"(like .xml, .json, .manifest, .ini), static assets, build scripts "
        f"(like .csproj, .sln), and documentation.\n\n"
        f"Return ONLY a YAML list of the file indices that should be documented as code modules.\n\n"
        f"```yaml\n- 0\n- 1\n- 3\n```"
    )

The function guarantees strict index-based mapping constraints by embedding explicit negative rules (excluding .xaml, .json, .csproj, etc.) alongside a standardized YAML code block schema. This format simplifies regex or YAML parsing downstream in nodes.py.

docs.title: build_chapter_summary_prompt()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def build_chapter_summary_prompt(chapter_num: int, abstraction_name: str, chapter_content: str, language: str = "english") -> str:

Description: Builds a structured summarization prompt designed to compress a generated chapter into a dense technical brief across four specific architectural dimensions. The resulting summary is passed into subsequent chapter prompts to maintain cross-chapter coherence without exhausting model context budgets.

Parameters: * chapter_num (int): The sequence number of the chapter being summarized. * abstraction_name (str): The title or abstraction boundary covered by the chapter. * chapter_content (str): The full Markdown content of the generated chapter. * language (str, optional): The target natural language for the output summary. Defaults to "english".

Returns: * str: The complete prompt payload for cross-chapter context generation.

Raises: * None.

Example: 

def build_chapter_summary_prompt(chapter_num: int, abstraction_name: str, chapter_content: str, language: str = "english") -> str:
    """Build the prompt for generating a technical summary of a written chapter."""
    lang_instruction = f"Write the entire summary in {language.capitalize()}. " if language.lower() != "english" else ""
    return (
        f"{lang_instruction}"
        f"Summarize the following documentation chapter as a structured technical brief. "
        f"For EACH of the 4 points below, write 3-5 concise technical sentences:\n\n"
        f"(1) **Component Scope & Responsibility**: What is the main technical domain this "
        f"chapter covers? What problems does it solve and what role does it play in the system?\n\n"
        f"(2) **Key Technical Elements**: What are the specific classes, services, functions, "
        f"data models, or protocols discussed? Name them and describe their concrete roles.\n\n"
        f"(3) **Implementation Patterns & Architecture**: What design patterns, communication "
        f"protocols, data flow strategies, error handling mechanisms, or security measures "
        f"are covered? How are they implemented?\n\n"
        f"(4) **System Integration & Dependencies**: How does this component interface with "
        f"other parts of the system? What does it consume from or provide to other components? "
        f"What are the key integration points?\n\n"
        f"---\n"
        f"Chapter {chapter_num}: {abstraction_name}\n"
        f"{chapter_content}"
    )

The function dynamically prepends a localization instruction when language is not English, ensuring consistent summarization across multi-language documentation runs. By constraining each dimension to 3–5 sentences, the prompt enforces information density and prevents unbounded token growth in downstream memory buffers managed by token_utils.py.

docs.title: build_mkdocs_config()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def build_mkdocs_config(site_name: str, nav_yaml: str) -> str:

Description: Assembles a complete mkdocs.yml configuration string optimized for the Material for MkDocs theme. The configuration includes code copy buttons, dark/light theme toggling, search, pan-zoom capabilities for Mermaid diagrams, Python Markdown syntax highlighting extensions, and custom superfences to support raw Mermaid diagram rendering.

Parameters: * site_name (str): The display title for the documentation website. * nav_yaml (str): A YAML-formatted navigation hierarchy string.

Returns: * str: The complete serialized YAML content for the mkdocs.yml file.

Raises: * None.

Example: 

def build_mkdocs_config(site_name: str, nav_yaml: str) -> str:
    """Build a complete mkdocs.yml for local --mkdocs output."""
    # Extract nav items from nav_snippet (strip the "nav:" header line)
    nav_lines = nav_yaml.split("\n")
    nav_body = "\n".join(nav_lines[1:]) if nav_lines else ""

    return (
        f"site_name: '{site_name}'\n"
        f"theme:\n"
        f"  name: material\n"
        f"  features:\n"
        f"    - content.code.copy\n"
        f"    - navigation.indexes\n"
        f"  palette:\n"
        f"    - scheme: default\n"
        f"      toggle:\n"
        f"        icon: material/brightness-7\n"
        f"        name: Switch to dark mode\n"
        f"    - scheme: slate\n"
        f"      toggle:\n"
        f"        icon: material/brightness-4\n"
        f"        name: Switch to light mode\n"
        f"plugins:\n"
        f"  - search\n"
        f"  - panzoom:\n"
        f"      include_selectors:\n"
        f"        - '.mermaid-raw'\n"
        f"markdown_extensions:\n"
        f"  - pymdownx.highlight:\n"
        f"      anchor_linenums: true\n"
        f"      use_pygments: true\n"
        f"  - pymdownx.superfences:\n"
        f"      custom_fences:\n"
        f"        - name: mermaid\n"
        f"          class: mermaid-raw\n"
        f"          format: !!python/name:pymdownx.superfences.fence_code_format\n"
        f"  - pymdownx.inlinehilite\n"
        f"extra_javascript:\n"
        f"  - https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/mermaid@11/dist/mermaid.min.js\n"
        f"  - javascripts/mermaid-init.js\n"
        f"nav:\n"
        f"  - Home: index.md\n"
        f"{nav_body}\n"
    )

The function parses the incoming nav_yaml string by stripping any top-level nav: declaration to prevent key duplication. It maps pymdownx.superfences to assign the .mermaid-raw CSS class instead of .mermaid, preventing MkDocs Material from overriding diagram color palettes.

docs.title: build_mermaid_init_js()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def build_mermaid_init_js() -> str:

Description: Constructs an inline vanilla JavaScript initializer string to be written to javascripts/mermaid-init.js. This script resolves DOM compatibility issues between pymdownx.superfences and the Mermaid rendering engine, while preserving Mermaid's default styling.

Parameters: * None.

Returns: * str: Executable JavaScript source code contained in an Immediately Invoked Function Expression (IIFE).

Raises: * None.

Example: 

def build_mermaid_init_js() -> str:
    """Build JS to initialize Mermaid on .mermaid-raw elements."""
    return """\
// Initialize Mermaid on .mermaid-raw elements (bypasses Material theme override)
// Material for MkDocs targets .mermaid class for its own color overrides.
// By using .mermaid-raw, diagrams render with Mermaid's default theme:
// yellow subgraph backgrounds, lavender nodes, clean rectangles.
//
// pymdownx.superfences fence_code_format wraps content as:
//   <pre class="mermaid-raw"><code>flowchart TD ...</code></pre>
// Mermaid expects the diagram text directly in the target element,
// so we unwrap the <code> child before calling mermaid.run().
(function() {
  function initMermaid() {
    if (typeof mermaid === 'undefined') return;
    try {
      // Unwrap: move <code> text content up to <pre> and remove <code>
      document.querySelectorAll('pre.mermaid-raw > code').forEach(function(code) {
        var pre = code.parentElement;
        pre.textContent = code.textContent;
      });
      mermaid.initialize({
        startOnLoad: false,
        theme: 'default',
        securityLevel: 'loose'
      });
      mermaid.run({ querySelector: '.mermaid-raw' }).catch(function(err) {
        console.warn('Mermaid render error:', err);
      });
    } catch (e) {
      console.warn('Mermaid init error:', e);
    }
  }
  if (document.readyState === 'loading') {
    document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', initMermaid);
  } else {
    initMermaid();
  }
})();
"""

The returned script unwraps inner <code> elements generated by pymdownx.superfences (<pre class="mermaid-raw"><code>...</code></pre>), moving text directly into the parent <pre> node. It configures mermaid.initialize with startOnLoad: false and securityLevel: 'loose', invoking mermaid.run() explicitly across all .mermaid-raw selectors.

docs.title: build_grouped_nav()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def build_grouped_nav(sections: list, chapter_files: list, indent: int = 4) -> list[str]:

Description: Recursively constructs indented YAML navigation entries from hierarchical section groupings and a list of generated chapter files. It matches modules to their source file metadata and groups sub-directory files into structured navigation levels while keeping root-level files flat.

Parameters: * sections (list): A list of dictionary objects defining section names, nested child sections, and assigned module names. * chapter_files (list): A list of metadata dictionaries containing module_name, filename, and original_path mappings. * indent (int, optional): Indentation space count for the current recursion level. Defaults to 4.

Returns: * list[str]: A list of formatted YAML navigation lines.

Raises: * None.

docs.title: Phase 1: Section Traversal & Child Processing
docs.text:
lines = []
    pad = " " * indent
    for section in sections:
        lines.append(f"{pad}- {section['name']}:")
        if "children" in section:
            lines.extend(build_grouped_nav(section["children"], chapter_files, indent + 2))
This phase creates the top-level section header and recursively processes any nested structures defined in the children key, incrementing the indentation by 2 spaces per recursion level.

docs.title: Phase 2: Module Identification & Path Resolution
docs.text:
# Collect matched modules with directory info
        matched = []
        for mod_name in section.get("modules", []):
            match = next((cf for cf in chapter_files if cf["module_name"] == mod_name), None)
            if match:
                dir_path = os.path.dirname(match.get("original_path", "")) or ""
                matched.append((dir_path, mod_name, match))
The algorithm iterates through all module names declared in the current section, matching each against the chapter_files lookup list. For every match, os.path.dirname extracts the directory path from original_path, normalizing empty strings for root-level modules.

docs.title: Phase 3: Directory Grouping & YAML Emission
docs.text:
# Group by directory
        from collections import defaultdict

        dir_groups = defaultdict(list)
        for dir_path, mod_name, match in matched:
            dir_groups[dir_path].append((mod_name, match))

        # Emit dir sub-layers for non-root dirs, flat for root files
        has_non_root = any(d for d in dir_groups)
        if has_non_root:
            for dir_path in sorted(dir_groups.keys()):
                if dir_path:
                    # Non-root: add directory sub-layer with bare module names
                    lines.append(f"{pad}  - {dir_path}:")
                    for mod_name, match in dir_groups[dir_path]:
                        lines.append(f"{pad}    - '{mod_name}': 'api/{match['filename']}'")
                else:
                    # Root files: flat (no sub-layer)
                    for mod_name, match in dir_groups[dir_path]:
                        lines.append(f"{pad}  - '{mod_name}': 'api/{match['filename']}'")
        else:
            # All root files → flat list
            for _dir_path, mod_name, match in matched:
                lines.append(f"{pad}  - '{mod_name}': 'api/{match['filename']}'")

    return lines
Matched modules are organized into directory buckets using collections.defaultdict. If any module belongs to a sub-directory, non-root paths are emitted as nested directory nodes with their contained files indented below. Root files remain flat at the section level.

docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def collect_all_modules(sections: list) -> set:

Description: Recursively traverses a section hierarchy tree to extract every referenced module name into a flat set.

Returns: * set: A set of all distinct module name strings found across the section tree.

def collect_all_modules(sections: list) -> set:
    """Recursively collect all module names referenced in a sections tree."""
    result = set()
    for section in sections:
        result.update(section.get("modules", []))
        if "children" in section:

This helper aggregates module identifiers across arbitrary nesting depths. It is used to validate that all documented files have been assigned to navigation sections without omissions or duplicates.

docs.title: Error Handling
docs.text:
• Missing Keys in Dictionaries: build_grouped_nav() and collect_all_modules() defensively use .get("modules", []), section.get("children"), and match.get("original_path", "") to avoid KeyError exceptions when handling incomplete dictionary structures.
  • Empty Navigation YAML: build_mkdocs_config() handles empty or single-line nav_yaml strings without raising IndexError by slicing nav_lines[1:] and checking collection truthiness before joining lines.
  • Client-Side Rendering Errors: build_mermaid_init_js() wraps diagram unwrapping, initialization, and execution within try...catch blocks and appends a .catch() handler to the mermaid.run() Promise. This ensures that a single invalid diagram does not break the documentation site or halt browser execution.

docs.title: Technical Overview
docs.text:
The utils.token_utils module provides utility functions for estimating, counting, and logging token consumption across prompt construction and node execution within the Codebase-Knowledge-Builder pipeline.

Accurate token tracking is critical for LLM-based pipelines to prevent exceeding model context windows, calculate workload budgets, and provide observability during graph execution. This module encapsulates interaction with the tiktoken library using the cl100k_base encoding (standard for modern OpenAI models like GPT-4 and GPT-3.5 Turbo), while implementing defensive fallbacks (character-based heuristic estimation) in the event that tiktoken fails or encounters an unhandled runtime exception. Additionally, it formats and outputs human-readable ANSI colored logs for the console alongside machine-parseable structured entries for the shared llm_logger.

docs.title: _get_encoding()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private (Internal Helper) Signature: def _get_encoding() -> tiktoken.Encoding | None:

Description: Implements lazy-loaded singleton initialization for the cl100k_base tiktoken tokenizer. If _encoding has not yet been initialized, it attempts to load the tokenizer via tiktoken.get_encoding("cl100k_base"). If an exception occurs (for example, missing vocabulary files, network issues downloading tokenizer assets, or environment mismatches), the exception is caught silently and _encoding remains None. Subsequent calls reuse the cached instance stored in the module-level _encoding global.

Parameters: * None.

Returns: * tiktoken.Encoding | None: The initialized cl100k_base encoding instance if successful, or None if loading failed.

Raises: * No exceptions are raised; errors during encoding initialization are caught internally.

Example: 

def _get_encoding():
    global _encoding
    if _encoding is None:
        try:
            _encoding = tiktoken.get_encoding("cl100k_base")
        except Exception:
            _encoding = None
    return _encoding

The function handles runtime robustness by wrapping the external library call in a generic try...except block. This guarantees that token counting features degrade gracefully to character-ratio heuristics rather than throwing fatal runtime errors during pipeline execution.

docs.title: count_tokens()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def count_tokens(text: str) -> int:

Description: Counts the number of tokens in a provided string using the cl100k_base encoding scheme via tiktoken. If the input string is empty or falsy, it immediately returns 0. When the encoding is successfully resolved through _get_encoding(), it invokes enc.encode() with disallowed_special=() to ensure that special tokens (e.g., <|endoftext|>) within codebase files are treated as raw text rather than raising syntax or encoding errors. If tiktoken is unavailable or _get_encoding() returned None, it falls back to a standard heuristic estimation dividing character length by 4 (len(text) // 4).

Parameters: * text (str): The raw text or prompt string to evaluate.

Returns: * int: Estimated or exact token count representing the string length in the cl100k_base vocabulary.

Raises: * No exceptions raised.

Example: 

def count_tokens(text: str) -> int:
    """Count tokens using tiktoken, with fallback to chars/4."""
    if not text:
        return 0
    enc = _get_encoding()
    if enc:
        return len(enc.encode(text, disallowed_special=()))
    return len(text) // 4

This method is central to all prompt size validations across pipeline nodes. Setting disallowed_special=() is critical when analyzing code repositories, as code frequently contains literal tokens (like <|endoftext|>, docstrings, or template syntax) that would otherwise cause standard tiktoken.encode() calls to throw a ValueError.

docs.title: log_token_estimation()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def log_token_estimation(node_name: str, prompt_content: str, max_tokens: int, token_usage: dict | None = None) -> None:

Description: Calculates total token volume for a node's prompt content, evaluates capacity utilization against max_tokens, formats optional per-section usage metrics, and dispatches log information to both stdout (via ANSI colored formatting) and the persistent logging backend (logger.info). When token_usage is provided as a dictionary of sub-component names and integer counts, it calculates the percentage of total tokens each component represents, aligns labels dynamically, and appends a structured breakdown to the output.

Parameters: * node_name (str): The identifier or name of the executing graph node (e.g., generate_readme, analyze_code). * prompt_content (str): The full constructed prompt string sent to the model. * max_tokens (int): The maximum context window or token budget allocated for the operation. * token_usage (dict | None, optional): Optional breakdown dictionary mapping section labels (e.g., 'System Prompt', 'Context Files') to their respective token counts. Defaults to None.

Returns: * None

Raises: * No exceptions raised. Zero-division guards are applied when calculating percentage capacity (max_tokens) and component percentages (token_count).

Example: 

def log_token_estimation(node_name: str, prompt_content: str, max_tokens: int, token_usage: dict | None = None) -> None:
    token_count = count_tokens(prompt_content)
    percentage = (token_count / max_tokens) * 100 if max_tokens else 0

    # Build token usage string if provided
    usage_str = ""
    usage_log_str = ""
    if token_usage:
        # Find the longest label for alignment
        max_label_len = max(len(label) for label in token_usage)
        lines = []
        log_parts = []
        for label, value in token_usage.items():
            pct = (value / token_count * 100) if token_count else 0
            padded_label = label.ljust(max_label_len)
            lines.append(f"\t{padded_label} : {value:,} ({pct:.0f}%)")
            log_parts.append(f"{label}={value:,} ({pct:.0f}%)")
        usage_str = "\n" + "\n".join(lines)
        usage_log_str = " | " + " | ".join(log_parts)

    # Console output (yellow) with token usage on separate lines
    print(f"\033[93m[Token Analytics] {node_name}: {token_count:,} / {max_tokens:,} tokens ({percentage:.1f}% capacity){usage_str}\033[0m")

    # File log stays single-line for parseability
    logger.info(f"NODE EXEC | node={node_name} | prompt_tokens={token_count:,} / {max_tokens:,} ({percentage:.1f}% capacity){usage_log_str}")

The function bifurcates the output destination: terminal users receive high-visibility ANSI yellow formatted logs (\033[93m...) with multi-line tab-aligned sub-metrics for clear visual inspection during CLI runs, while logger.info() receives a single-line delimited string (NODE EXEC | node=... | prompt_tokens=...) optimal for downstream log ingestion, regex filtering, and monitoring systems.

docs.title: token_utils.py
docs.text:
Source: utils/token_utils.py

Following the prompt construction and site configuration routines defined in prompts.py, the system must measure, budget, and log token consumption across prompt payloads before dispatching inference requests or persisting artifacts. The utils/token_utils.py module provides the centralized token estimation, context window budgeting, and telemetry logging layer for the Codebase-Knowledge-Builder system.

docs.title: Technical Overview
docs.text:
The primary responsibility of utils/token_utils.py is to calculate prompt token volume accurately while ensuring zero runtime interruption if external tokenizer components fail. It acts as an operational bridge between workflow orchestration nodes in nodes.py, the LLM inference gateway in call_llm.py, and the terminal/log dispatch system in output.py. The module wraps OpenAI's tiktoken library with lazy-loaded singleton initialization and a fallback heuristic calculation based on character count.

Beyond scalar token counting, the module provides multi-channel telemetry through log_token_estimation(). It computes the prompt's percentage utilization against the target model's configured context window ceiling, formats granular per-component breakdowns (e.g., system instructions, repository file slices, chapter summaries), and simultaneously dispatches formatted terminal notifications via emit() and structured, single-line log entries to the llm_logger file stream.
